acceptance_criteria: Human management can assign, transfer and clear a single ant owner and override membership or messenger choices. The current owner can add/remove ant members and set/clear the messenger only for its own channel. Non-owners cannot manage a channel; former owners lose authority after transfer or removal. Ant ownership grants neither ownership-transfer nor channel-deletion permission and grants no direct channel KV write access. Ownership does not change mention/messenger wake rules or human thread ownership and escalation. Concurrent management requests cannot overwrite unrelated changes or use stale ownership to bypass authorization. Focused tests cover authorized management, rejected operations, transfer/revocation and existing ownerless behavior. README documents ownership, role separation, management commands and permissions.

description: Give a channel an optional single ant owner, separate from its messenger and members. Humans assign, transfer or clear ownership and retain override authority. The owner may add or remove ant members and set or clear the messenger of its own channel, but may not transfer ownership or delete the channel. Ownership alone does not wake the owner on every post. Channel ownership remains distinct from human thread ownership and escalation.
design: Keep channel KV writes restricted to human credentials under the current contract. Introduce authenticated, validated management requests with a trusted mutation path rather than granting ants unrestricted channel KV writes. Authorize against the current owner and preserve concurrent-update protections. Define the trusted request processor, permission boundaries, revocation behavior and ant-facing management interface before implementation. Update affected canonical requirements through bd spec change before changing existing human-only management behavior. Channels without an owner retain current behavior; owning, triaging and participating are independent roles.
title: Ant channel ownership with scoped management and human override

title: Ant daemon
The daemon acks an inbox message only after its reply is stored in JetStream.

While a message is in hand (waiting or prompting) the daemon sends progress acks at a third of the ack wait, so a crash or dead link redelivers it within the ack wait (60 s) and a redelivery of a message still in hand is not prompted again.

Usage first passing [storage] warn_percent (default 80, 0 never) of a store's known limit sends the default human one notice per crossing, naming the three streams using most and the setting to raise, with a level-0 storage escalation so push sinks deliver it: the daemon creating note _storage.<domain|_>.<store>.warned in ants_sessions sends it, so several daemons and restarts send one, and the note is deleted once usage falls more than 5 points below the share.

A message an ant sent that still waits (no mark, or started) 15 minutes after sending, for an ant absent from the roster for 15 minutes, is told of once to the thread owner, else the default human, by the sending ant's daemon reading its sentread-<ant> consumer, listing the messages, naming ants withdraw and suggesting up to five live ants sharing the absent one's capabilities; creating <sender>.unserved.<id> in ants_attempts first makes it once across watchers and restarts.

An ant acts on the first decision on its tool request: a human's as stream ANTS stored it on the request's decision subject, read back with a direct get, never one heard but refused by the stream, or an ant's from its own escalate_to, unless a human's is stored by the time the ant's arrives; a stream or credentials without direct gets fall back to the first human decision heard, with a warning.

At startup the daemon waits for an unreachable NATS server, retrying refused, timed-out or unresolved connections with backoff capped at 30 s and a warning per attempt, and stops on Ctrl-C or SIGTERM meanwhile; rejected credentials, an unreadable credentials file, a malformed URL or a TLS error fail the persona at once.

A prompt past its time limit or tool call limit, or a thread or persona past its token or cost cap, is cancelled with ACP session/cancel, replied to with a notice and handed to the human like a spent turn budget; a message from the human renews the thread allowance, the persona daily allowance renews at 00:00 UTC, and spend survives daemon and harness restarts.

Before prompting, the daemon marks the attempt as started in KV ants_attempts under the persona and the message's stream sequence; a later delivery of a started message is prompted with a warning that tools may already have run, and one whose reply was already recorded re-sends that reply under a message id made of persona and sequence and is acked without another prompt.

Each served persona is registered in KV ants_roster with machine, harness, capabilities, activity (idle, or working while a message is handled) and counts of messages being handled and live harnesses, refreshed with each heartbeat and at once on turning idle or working; it expires when heartbeats stop, and entries without the activity fields still parse.

While prompting, the daemon publishes the thread's state, the harness's streamed reply text and thoughts (joined for up to 250 ms), tool calls as they start or change status, and its plan to ants.status.<persona>.<thread> on core NATS; an update that cannot be sent at once is dropped, never holding up the harness or an ack.
A message whose last allowed attempt fails or never finishes is kept on ants.dead.<persona> and the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, is told; a human can replay or drop it.

A prompt past its time limit or tool call limit, or a thread or persona past its token or cost cap, is cancelled with ACP session/cancel, replied to with a notice and handed to the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, like a spent turn budget; a message from any human renews the thread allowance, the persona daily allowance renews at 00:00 UTC, and spend survives daemon and harness restarts.

The daemon config key 'human' names the default human (default 'human'), who gets the escalations and notices of threads with no owner; the daemon tells humans by the ants_humans registry, which it watches and, while the bucket is missing, looks for again periodically.

A persona acts only on the approval decision stream ANTS stored on the request's decision subject, read back with a direct get, never on a decision it hears but the stream refused; a stream or credentials without direct gets fall back to the first decision heard, with a warning.

A message whose last allowed attempt fails or never finishes is kept on ants.dead.<persona> and its notice escalates up the persona's escalate_to chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human; a human can replay or drop it.

A prompt past its time limit or tool call limit, or a thread or persona past its token or cost cap, is cancelled with ACP session/cancel, replied to with a notice and escalated like a spent turn budget; a message from any human, or once per escalation level the escalation leader's answer, renews the thread allowance, the persona daily allowance renews at 00:00 UTC, and spend survives daemon and harness restarts.

The persona config keys escalate_to (other personas, no duplicates, the first leads), max_escalation_hops (default 3) and escalate_after_secs (default 1800, 0 waits indefinitely) set the persona's escalation chain, which its roster entry publishes.

An escalation fans out to every unvisited member of the chain on ants.inbox.<member>.<persona> with the escalation attached, naming the stuck thread, the reason, the level and the leader; a member stuck while working on it, or the persona stuck again after the leader's answer, sends it one level higher through the leader's escalate_to from the roster, and an empty chain, a visited target or a level past max_escalation_hops sends it to the thread's owner, else the default human.

A message on the stuck thread from the escalation's leader, carrying the escalation, gives the thread a fresh turn budget and allowance at most once per level, a non-leader's does not, and only a human's message ends the escalation so the next one starts at the persona's own chain; the level, its renewal and its deadline live with the thread's spend in ants_sessions and survive restarts.

A thread's origin chain is the escalate_to of the thread's creator when an ant other than the stuck one created it, else the stuck ant's: a fresh escalation of such a thread starts at level 0 led by the creator, with the stuck ant and then the creator visited, so the hop limit counts from the creator's chain, a chain back to either goes to the owner, and the creator itself is never sent it.
Channel ownership never selects or redirects a thread's escalation: an ant-created thread's escalation ends at a human who took the thread as its owner, else the stuck ant's daemon's default human.

On SIGHUP the daemon reloads its config file: it starts the ants newly listed, stops those no longer listed as on Ctrl-C (prompts in flight finish, waiting messages are handed back unacked), stops those whose resolved settings changed the same way and serves them again with the new settings once stopped, starts again a listed ant that had failed, and leaves the others running untouched; a file that fails to load is logged and the ants served stay as they were.

With the ant config key worktrees each thread works in its own git worktree <home>/worktrees/<thread> on branch ants/<ant>/<thread>, created on its first prompt, reused when its harness starts again and removed once its session expired and no harness of it is live, keeping a branch with unmerged commits; a workdir outside a git work tree stays shared, and a worktree that cannot be created leaves the thread in the shared workdir with a warning.

Config [[schedule]] entries (a 5-field cron in UTC or an every interval anchored at the Unix epoch, an ant or a channel, literal text, an optional owner) make ants daemon, when serving the whole file, send each firing as a new thread under the schedule's own webhook-role credentials, once across daemons and restarts by its key <schedule>.<unix time> in ants_webhooks and its Nats-Msg-Id; a firing more than a minute late is skipped, never made up.

A human's cancel request stops the prompt running on its thread with ACP session/cancel, the same way as a prompt limit; the reply carries the partial output and an [ants] notice naming the human, the message is acked as answered with no retry, dead letter or escalation, and the messages waiting behind it on the thread still run.
A daemon keeps what each thread spent since a human's last message on it and what the ant spent each UTC day in ants_sessions whether or not the ant has caps.
The thread-to-session map lives in KV ants_sessions and survives a daemon restart.

With worktrees off, thread worktrees left under <home>/worktrees are removed the same way once their session expired and no harness of their thread is live, with git run in the repository the worktrees belong to, and no new worktree is created.

When the harness is signed out, the daemon holds the message in hand first on its thread without counting an attempt or redelivering it, starts no further prompts, tells the thread owner (else the default human) directly once per signed-out period with the sign-in command and machine, checks the harness with a handshake every minute and answers the held messages once one succeeds.

While the harness is signed out, the ant's roster entry carries signed_out with since and the sign-in command, shown by ants roster and list_ants and ranked last by route; it is published at once and cleared once a handshake finds the harness signed in again, and entries without it still parse.

ants daemon, ants channel serve, ants webhook serve and ants bridge check every 30 s (--upgrade-check, 0 never) whether another file replaced their executable at the path found at start, or it was rewritten; once the new file is executable, non-empty and unchanged across two checks, the daemon stops its ants as on SIGTERM, prompts in flight finishing, the others stop at once, and the process exits with status 75, which the contrib units restart on.

With --metrics ADDR or a metrics config key, ants daemon, ants webhook serve and ants bridge serve plain HTTP on ADDR, off by default and warned about off loopback: GET /healthz answers 200 while the NATS connections the process needs are up (a daemon: at least one ant served, all connected), else 503; GET /metrics answers Prometheus text with ants_ gauges and _total counters for connection state, harnesses, prompts in flight, retries, dead letters and spend per ant.

A tool request left undecided until it expires is rejected, and before the ant goes on the thread's owner, else the default human, gets a message on the thread naming the ant, request, tool and thread and how to retry ('ants ask --thread'), raise approval_timeout or add an allow rule.

When the harness reports a provider limit, the daemon holds the message in hand first on its thread without counting an attempt or redelivering it, starts no prompts until a backoff passes (30s doubling to 10min for a rate limit, 15min doubling to 2h for an exhausted quota, a hint replacing the doubling within the cap), and tells the owner (else the default human) of an exhausted quota once until a message gets past a limit.

While a provider limit holds the messages, the ant's roster entry carries limited with kind (rate_limit or quota), since and until, shown by ants roster, list_ants and the ants ask warning and ranked by route after ants without one; it is cleared when the wait passes, and entries without it, or with an unknown kind, still parse.

When session/load fails, the daemon starts a new session, logs it and stores its id, and the first prompt in it carries an [ants] line saying the context was rebuilt and the thread's history read back from ANTS with the ant's credentials: messages to the ant before the one answered, the ant's own messages, notes and channel posts on the thread, oldest first, the most recent within 64 KiB with the older ones counted, or an [ants] line saying it could not be read.

A prompt that outgrows the model's context window runs again once in a new session seeded with the thread's history and an [ants] line saying why, without spending a delivery attempt; one that outgrows a new session too is not retried, but escalated with reason context_window and the harness's error, and its message acked without a dead letter.

One daemon process can serve several personas, each with its own NATS credentials.

The daemon also reloads its config file exactly as on SIGHUP once the file changed on disk (modification time, length or inode, checked every 3 s on its own runtime, with no watcher thread) and stayed unchanged across two checks; a reload by SIGHUP counts as having read the file, and a file that fails to load leaves the ants served as they were.

When session/load fails, the daemon starts a new session, logs it and stores its id, and the first prompt in it carries an [ants] line saying the context was rebuilt and the thread's history read back from ANTS with the ant's credentials: messages to the ant before the one answered, the ant's own messages, notes and channel posts on the thread, oldest first, the most recent within the history budget, or an [ants] line saying it could not be read.

A rebuilt session's history budget is the ant's history_budget, else its context value's or one derived from that value's window, else the harness's history_budget or one derived from its window (a twelfth of the window at 4 bytes a token), else 64 KiB; never above a quarter of the window, and halved after a context overflow.

A rebuilt session's history cuts each entry to an eighth of the budget, and an [ants] line before it tells how many older entries of each kind were left out, their senders and the time span they cover, without a model call.

Config [[schedule]] entries (a 5-field cron in UTC or a zone, or an every interval from the epoch, an ant or a channel, literal text, optional owner and catch_up) make ants daemon, serving the whole file, send each firing as a new thread under the schedule's webhook-role credentials, once across daemons and restarts by its key <schedule>.<unix time> in ants_webhooks and its Nats-Msg-Id; a firing over a minute late is skipped, but with catch_up the latest missed in 7 days goes out late, marked.

A schedule's cron reads in the local time of the IANA zone its timezone names, else the config file's top-level timezone, else UTC, an unknown name failing the config load: a local time skipped when daylight saving time begins fires once, at the end of the gap, and one repeated when it ends fires once, at its first occurrence.

ants and ants-daemon build for Windows (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and -msvc) with no service units: the daemon stops on Ctrl-C, Ctrl-Break, the console closing or system shutdown as on SIGTERM, has no SIGHUP reload, and files kept at mode 0600 elsewhere inherit their directory's access list.

A message whose last allowed attempt fails or never finishes is kept on ants.dead.<ant> and its notice escalates up the thread's origin chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human; the human-side max-deliveries backstop tells that owner, else the default human, directly, with a level-0 dead_letter escalation so 'ants webhook serve' pushes it and 'ants thread list --escalated' lists it, but no reminder; a human can replay or drop it.

Config [[ant_template]] entries set harnesses, models each with its highest reasoning effort (low < medium < high < xhigh < max), contexts, ceilings on an ant's thread and daily caps, max_harnesses, prompt_timeout and max_tool_calls, fixed allow rules and named allow sets, max_ants, managers (exact ant names, none by default) and a name pattern; an unknown key fails the config load.

An [[ant]] carrying template and added_by takes from the template every setting a request may not choose, escalates to the manager that added it, never manages a template itself, and is checked against the current template at load and on reload: a choice outside an allowlist, over a ceiling, past max_ants or off the name pattern fails the load with an error naming the bound.
A message whose last allowed attempt fails or never finishes is kept on ants.dead.<persona> and the human is told; the human can replay or drop it.

The ants added from a template with pool_daily_cost or pool_daily_tokens share that UTC-day cap on top of their own, summed from each member's daily spend in ants_sessions so it holds across daemons and restarts: an ant reaching it is cancelled, notified and escalated as at its daily cap, and spend first passing spend_warn_percent of it warns once per UTC day.

A daemon serving a whole config file adds a requested ant by generating its key locally (the seed never leaves the machine), writing its signed credentials, and appending its `[[ant]]` entry with `template` and `added_by`, which the file reload then serves; one request at a time per process.

A daemon creates the message mark <ant>.msg.<id> in ants_attempts as started before anything runs for a message, so a human withdrawal created there first wins; a withdrawn message, on any delivery, is acked without prompting the harness once a withdrawn notice is stored on its thread, and the running prompt and other queued messages continue.

The daemon serving an ant answers a QueueRequest on ants.queue.<ant> with the messages in its hands (running, waiting their turn, or held for sign-in or a provider limit) and the inbox consumer delivered sequence and pending count; a standby daemon does not answer.

Each harness start puts the agent the harness named itself as in ACP initialize (agent_info) into the ant's roster entry as agent with name and version, published at once when it changes and shown by list_ants; it is missing until a harness started, and entries without it still parse.

After 3 harness start failures within 10 minutes on at least 2 threads with no start succeeding between, the daemon holds messages without spending attempts, sets failing (since, last error) in the ant's roster entry, tells the thread's owner, else the default human, once with a level-0 harness escalation naming ants harness check, and starts the harness every minute until it starts, then clears failing and lets the messages go on.

A thread a webhook or schedule starts is narrowed to the allow rules of its [[webhook]] or [[schedule]] entry, else to read-only rules (read:*, search, think and the ants tools that read or message other ants): the ant's daemon auto-approves a tool call on it only when both those rules and the ant's allowlist allow it, and allow = ["*"] opts out.

A thread's narrowed tool rules travel on its messages and posts (allow), kept by replies, spin-offs, channel posts, escalations and approval requests, and are stored per thread in ants_sessions, across restarts, until a human's message to the ant on the thread lifts them; carried rules only narrow, never widen, an ant's allowlist.

Unless the config sets redact = false, the daemon replaces secrets with [redacted] in tool requests (before cutting their input), status streams (never split across updates), replies, escalations, notes and MCP sends and posts: values (8+ chars, not paths) of its env, the ant's and the harness's whose name looks secret or, for the latter two, that look like a token, and secret patterns (private keys, Bearer tokens, cloud, GitHub and chat tokens, NKey seeds, JWTs, URL passwords).

Every 5 minutes (first 30 s after start) one ant of each daemon process per NATS server reads the account's JetStream usage on the hub and, through a leaf node, on the leaf node, against each store's limit (the account's, else [storage] max_file_store and max_memory_store for the hub, else the limits ants leaf config writes), and serves it as gauges ants_jetstream_bytes and ants_jetstream_limit_bytes with labels domain and store.

acceptance_criteria: All six audit findings have an explicit implemented resolution and documented CLI/configuration grammar. Resetting the channel messenger uses --default-messenger and still selects the default messenger. ask and post consistently distinguish first-reply waiting from streaming, support documented timeouts and terminate correctly on timeout or interruption. Duration flags follow one convention with documented units and focused parsing tests. Default and per-ant harness settings use consistent terminology; built-in messenger enablement is explicitly configurable independently of harness selection. ants notes reads/posts passive thread notes without waking ants; execution plans remain distinct. Tool requests expose consistent list/show/approve/reject operations without changing authorization or decision precedence; enrollment operations remain clearly separate. Replaced spellings need no compatibility aliases. close_reason: Leaf JetStream outbox ANTS_OUT, sourced by hub ANTS_IN then ANTS per machine/persona; publish falls back to the outbox when the hub stream is unreachable; 'ants leaf outbox' sets it up. Follow-ups ants-fv1, ants-1at, ants-5zr, ants-xyb, ants-78l, ants-7tn. Merged in af344df.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-862695e4
comments.text:
Design (branch fleet/leaf-buffer): each leaf runs JetStream in the machine's own domain with one stream, ANTS_OUT (ants.out.>, file, 30 days). Clients (bus::store) publish to the hub stream as before; on 'no stream' or timeout they put the same message, same Nats-Msg-Id, on ants.out. locally (inbox messages, replies, plan posts without expected seq). Two hops on the hub, both JetStream sources pulled by the hub and resumed after outages/restarts: (1) intake ANTS_IN sources every outbox via external api $JS..API / deliver $JS.S., transforming > to ants.in..> so a machine cannot pose as another; (2) ANTS sources ANTS_IN per machine+persona with transforms only for what the persona may publish itself (inbox.*.

, plan.*.

; the human inbox.>), back to canonical subjects; the rest stays in ANTS_IN. Msg-id dedupe drops copies within the 2 min window. Setup: 'ants leaf outbox --persona ...' (human; --remove). Hub needs feature_flags { js_api_reply_v2: true } so source replies are $JSC.R...ANTS_OUT.... which the leaf may publish; human's setup connection uses inbox prefix _INBOX.human.leaf.. Uplink creds: + pub $JS.S..>, $JSC.R..*.ANTS_OUT.>, _INBOX.human.leaf..>; + sub $JS..API outbox stream/consumer ops and $JS.FC.ANTS_OUT.>; never ants.out.*. Spec: added h0k.12, changed h0k.8/9/10 -> h0k.13/15/14. Verified e2e in crates/ants/src/outbox.rs. Gotcha: hub stream interest crosses an uplink only via literal allowances (nats-server ReverseMatch), see ants-1at. Follow-ups: ants-fv1 ants-1at ants-5zr ants-xyb ants-78l ants-7tn.

description: With the uplink down, a publish to the hub stream from a leaf fails at once ('no stream found for given subject'); no store-and-forward. Options: ants retries with back-off, or a leaf-local stream sourced into the hub (JetStream sources/mirrors across domains). Found in ants-qjf.9.
title: Buffer publishes on a leaf node while the uplink is down

close_reason: New launchd agent ants.logrotate (contrib/launchd), installed by install-units.sh: hourly copy-truncate of *.log over 10 MiB, 5 gzipped copies kept. ants-ved.47.

Rotate them: install a newsyslog.d entry from scripts/install-units.sh, or have ants write and rotate its own log file under a size cap.

close_reason: [[schedule]] config with cron (UTC) or every interval, to ant or channel, sent by ants daemon under webhook-role creds; firings deduped via ants_webhooks key + Nats-Msg-Id, missed firings >1m skipped (8f7a3cb)

acceptance_criteria: A standby daemon starts serving an ant within about a second of the active daemon entry expiring, without polling. ants init upgrades existing buckets.
close_reason: Roster bucket leaves expiry markers (nats-server >= 2.11, added by ants init); a waiting daemon watches and takes over within ~1s, with a 60s safety poll, or every heartbeat on older hubs.
description: The roster (ROSTER_TTL 30s) and presence (PRESENCE_TTL 30s) buckets expire entries through the bucket max_age, which is silent: no watcher hears that an entry is gone. So a standby daemon in roster::wait_for_turn polls, and readers of a stale view (ants roster, notify Present) learn of a dead daemon or device only on their next read. nats-server 2.11 KV limit markers (ADR-48; async-nats kv::Config::limit_markers, which sets allow_msg_ttl and subject_delete_marker_ttl) put a delete marker with Nats-Marker-Reason: MaxAge when an entry expires, and watchers see it. Per-key TTLs (kv::Store::create_with_ttl / Nats-TTL; whole seconds only) could also give each entry its own lifetime. allow_msg_ttl can be turned on for an existing bucket (it cannot be turned off later), so hub::upgrade would add it as a Drift for the roster and presence buckets. The roster watch in roster.rs already filters on kv::Operation::Put, so check how a MaxAge marker shows up (Delete or Purge).
title: Use KV limit markers so roster and presence expiry is seen by watchers

close_reason: Ants and webhooks get no stream info of ants_sessions, ants_attempts or ants_owners; daemons use DirectKv (direct get + publish) so no ant can list other ants' thread ids; requirement ants-h0k.60; ANTS stream listing tracked in ants-38vp (3b81c1d).

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-004b8d48
comments.text: Terminology updated for ants-gqgs: persona -> ant (PersonaId -> UserId, ants persona add -> ants add).

description: Permissions::for_user grants $JS.API.STREAM.INFO.KV_ants_sessions (async-nats get_key_value needs it). A STREAM.INFO request with subjects_filter lists every key in the bucket, so an ant can see other ants' thread ids (not their session ids or values). Consider a bucket per ant, or opening the store without STREAM.INFO (async-nats get_stream_no_info + hand-built Store is not public), if thread ids must stay private.
title: Session bucket keys of other ants are listable via STREAM.INFO

close_reason: Uplink credentials include a literal subject per persona inbox/plan pattern so ReverseMatch finds them and hub stream interest crosses the leaf uplink without the human; upstream report drafted in a comment (59035d2)

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-720a8b14
comments.text:
Confirmed in nats-server v2.15.3 source and by test. Hub side: canSubscribeInternal (client.go ~3470) lets a wildcard subscription cross to a LEAF only if perms.sub.allow (= the uplink user's pub allow, swapped) Match()es it or, for wildcards, ReverseMatch()es it. reverseMatchLevel on '>' calls getAllNodes(l), which adds the l.pwc/l.fwc nodes themselves and recurses only into l.nodes, never into l.pwc.next / l.fwc.next. So the allowance 'ants.inbox.*.dev-a' is never found for 'ants.inbox.>' (nor 'ants.plan.*.

' for 'ants.plan.>', so plan interest never crossed, even with the human on the uplink). Local fix (commit 59035d2 on fleet/1at): Permissions::for_leaf adds, per persona, its sendable patterns with '*' replaced by the persona id (ants.inbox.dev-a.dev-a, ants.plan.dev-a.dev-a): literal subsets of what the patterns already allow, so nothing widens. Test in leaf.rs: dev-a-only uplink; direct bus::publish -> Stored::Hub and plan::publish(Some(0)) stored; dev-b (not on the uplink) still gets "no stream" at once (the leaf filters by the uplink's perms before forwarding); ANTS holds 2. Existing uplink creds need re-issuing (ants auth leaf). Upstream bug report draft (nats-io/nats-server): Title: Leafnode: hub wildcard interest not propagated when the leaf user's publish allow has '*' before its last token (ReverseMatch/getAllNodes skips pwc/fwc subtrees) Version: v2.15.3 Repro: hub.conf: port: 4222 leafnodes { port: 7422, authorization { users = [ { user: leaf, password: leaf, permissions: { publish: { allow: ["foo.*.bar"] }, subscribe: { allow: ["_INBOX.>"] } } } ] } } leaf.conf: port: 4223 leafnodes { remotes = [ { url: "nats://leaf:leaf@127.0.0.1:7422" } ] } 1. hub: nats -s nats://127.0.0.1:4222 sub 'foo.>' 2. leaf: nats -s nats://127.0.0.1:4223 pub foo.x.bar hi Result: nothing received on the hub (no LS+ for foo.> reaches the leaf; a request gets "no responders"). Adding the literal allow "foo.x.bar" makes it work; so does a hub sub on "foo.x.*" (literal path through reverseMatchLevel). Expected: foo.> interest crosses, since its subject space overlaps an allowed subject; the hub still checks each inbound LMSG against the permissions (leafMsgAllowed). Cause: server/sublist.go getAllNodes() adds l.pwc and l.fwc but does not recurse into l.pwc.next, so allowances below a '*' token are never reported by ReverseMatch for a '>' query. Suggested fix: in getAllNodes, `if l.pwc != nil { addNodeToResults(l.pwc, results); getAllNodes(l.pwc.next, results) }`.

description: nats-server 2.15.3 propagates the hub stream's interest (ants.inbox.>, ants.plan.>) to a leaf only if the uplink's publish allowances ReverseMatch it; ReverseMatch (sublist.go getAllNodes) misses allowances with '*' before the last token such as 'ants.inbox.*.dev-a'. Without human in the uplink credentials, a persona's direct publishes from the leaf find no stream and go through the outbox even with the uplink up (and before ants-0ul, failed outright unless a hub client had a narrower live subscription). Investigate: report upstream, or a different subject layout / extra allowance that matches without widening what the leaf may publish.
title: Let the hub stream's interest cross a leaf uplink without the human's allowances

close_reason: Unanswered escalations are reminded after escalation_reminder (default 4h), then daily for 30 days, by the active daemon only, and listed by ants thread list --escalated (ants-0mi.76, ants-ved.60).
description: An escalation reaching a human (turn_budget, cap, notes, dead_letter, asked) is sent once; nothing reminds the owner if no human answers. Remind after a configurable delay (and daily) through the inbox and push sinks, and list open escalations (e.g. ants thread list --escalated or an inbox section) until a human message on the thread resolves them.

close_reason: ants webhook notify-test HUMAN and doctor checks of webhook secrets (mode 0600), config and public_url, in 38adc52
description: A misconfigured ntfy, Slack or Telegram sink surfaces only when a real tool request or escalation fails to reach the human (failures are logged, not retried). Add a command (e.g. ants webhook notify-test HUMAN) that sends a test notice through each of the human's sinks and reports each result, and have ants doctor check sink configuration (secret files present and 0600, public_url reachable).

close_reason: ants post --wait/--follow reads back channel posts stored after its post every 5 s (human by STREAM.MSG.GET, ant via chanread spares), deduplicated by post id with the live subscription; ants-h0k.56 (5e8dd77)

title: ants post --wait/--follow on a leaf misses posts stored while its uplink is down

close_reason: Per-ant worktrees option: each thread gets its own git worktree (branch ants/<ant>/<thread>) under the ant home, reused on session/load, pruned hourly once the session expires; non-git workdirs share (33ffb82)

acceptance_criteria: An ant can start a channel thread and remains identifiable as its creator across replies and restarts. An ant-created thread uses the configured escalation chain of its creating ant without a new coordinator role; delegated work has a documented and tested origin-chain selection rule. Empty or exhausted chains, cycles and hop-limit exhaustion reach the configured default human rather than looping among ants. Existing turn budgets, escalation timeouts and once-per-level renewal protections remain enforced across restarts. Channel owner assignment or transfer does not redirect thread escalation. Existing human-owned threads and legacy threads remain compatible. Focused tests cover creator propagation, origin distinct from the stuck ant, multi-level escalation, human fallback and restart recovery. README and affected canonical requirements describe the resulting behavior.
close_reason: creator on Envelope/ChannelPost from the subject-checked top-level author (no humans, webhooks or channel manager), kept like owner; escalations on ant-created threads start at level 0 led by the creator, visited [stuck, creator]; MCP post_channel (member or messenger, no owner, turns left on the current message); ants post with ant creds creates; watch shows created by. Commits 3a941a6, e98e1ec.
description: Support channel threads started by an ant with permanent creator attribution and escalation through the existing escalate_to chain of the creating ant, ending at the configured default human when the chain is exhausted. Do not introduce a separate coordinator role or make an ant a human owner. Channel ownership remains limited to channel management and does not determine thread escalation.
design: Reuse existing escalation machinery, including chain lookup, leader progression, visited-target protection, max_escalation_hops, timeouts, turn budgets and persisted escalation state. Keep creator attribution distinct from the existing human owner field; retain compatibility with stored threads lacking creator metadata. Existing requirements start escalation from the stuck ant, which can differ from the creating ant: explicitly define origin-chain selection for work delegated to another ant and update affected requirements through bd spec change before changing that behavior. Preserve established human-owned thread behavior and human-only allowance renewal rules. No change to channel mention/messenger wake rules is implied.
title: Ant-created channel threads: creator attribution and existing escalation chain

description: The routing ant.
title: Messenger and planning
The messenger routes a request to personas by their roster capabilities.

antsd serves MCP tools post_plan and read_plan; each post spends one turn of the thread's budget, the post that spends the last one tells the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, and the room takes no more agent posts until a human posts there.
Agents plan together on ants.plan.<thread>, and the thread escalates up the persona's escalate_to chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, when its budget is spent.

antsd serves MCP tools post_plan and read_plan; each post spends one turn of the thread's budget, the post that spends the last one escalates the thread up the persona's escalate_to chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, and the room takes no more agent posts until a human posts there.

antsd serves MCP tools post_plan and read_plan; each post spends one turn of the thread's budget, the post that spends the last one escalates the thread up the persona's escalate_to chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, and the room takes no more agent posts until a human posts there or the escalation goes up a chain level, which posts there with a fresh turn budget once per level.

antsd serves MCP tools post_plan and read_plan on the thread's notes; each post spends one turn of the thread's budget, the post that spends the last one escalates the thread up the persona's escalate_to chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, and the notes take no more agent posts until a human posts there or the escalation goes up a chain level, which posts there with a fresh turn budget once per level.

CLI help, README and MCP tool descriptions call a thread's shared plan board its thread notes: one board per thread, whose posts notify and wake nobody and which agents read only by calling read_plan, while 'ants ask --thread' prompts only the named recipient; commands, MCP tool names and 'ants.plan' subjects keep the name plan.

A top-level provider in ~/.ants/config.toml is the default harness of the file's personas, and a daemon whose config sets it serves a built-in persona 'messenger' on the provider's defaults, unless the file defines a persona named messenger, which replaces it; a daemon serves the built-in messenger only while holding the messenger's roster entry: it waits while another daemon's messenger is listed, on any machine, and hands over once another daemon puts that entry.
The messenger routes a request to ants by their roster capabilities.
antsd serves MCP tools list_ants and route, so any ant finds others by roster capability; route sends to the first ant by name, other than the caller, that advertises the capability.

Each ant may configure an optional whoami field; the daemon includes the ant name and configured whoami in every harness prompt, including resumed sessions, publishes whoami in its roster entry, and exposes it through list_ants, while missing whoami remains compatible with older configurations and entries and capability routing stays unchanged.
Agents plan together on ants.plan.<thread>, and the thread goes to the human when its budget is spent.
Agents plan together on ants.plan.<thread>, and the thread escalates up the ant's escalate_to chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, when its budget is spent.

antsd serves MCP tools post_plan and read_plan on the thread's notes; each post spends one turn of the thread's budget, the post that spends the last one escalates the thread up the ant's escalate_to chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, and the notes take no more agent posts until a human posts there or the escalation goes up a chain level, which posts there with a fresh turn budget once per level.

A top-level provider in ~/.ants/config.toml is the default harness of the file's ants, and a daemon whose config sets it serves a built-in ant 'messenger' on the provider's defaults, unless the file defines an ant named messenger, which replaces it; a daemon serves the built-in messenger only while holding the messenger's roster entry: it waits while another daemon's messenger is listed, on any machine, and hands over once another daemon puts that entry.

A daemon serves a built-in ant 'messenger' on the defaults of its config file's top-level harness unless the file sets messenger = false or defines an ant named messenger, which replaces it; it serves the built-in messenger only while holding the messenger's roster entry: it waits while another daemon's messenger is listed, on any machine, and hands over once another daemon puts that entry.
A config file with messenger = false and no [[ant]] entries fails to load, as there is nothing to serve; one with neither keys nor [[ant]] entries serves only the built-in messenger.

A thread's shared board is its thread notes everywhere: one board per thread, whose posts notify and wake nobody, read by agents only with the MCP tool read_notes and posted to with post_notes, by humans with 'ants notes THREAD [TEXT]', on 'ants.notes' subjects; 'ants ask --thread' prompts only the named recipient, and the notes stay distinct from the execution plan an ant reports in its status, which 'ants watch' shows.

Agents coordinate in the thread notes on ants.notes.<thread>, and the thread escalates up the ant's escalate_to chain, ending at the thread's owner, else the daemon's default human, when its budget is spent.

description:
ants-ldc3 and ants-d42q verified the Linux Secret Service store (secret-tool) with GNOME Keyring, KDE Wallet and KeePassXC in Debian containers; no WSL 2 machine was reachable. On a Windows host with WSL 2 (Ubuntu 24.04 image), build or install ants for linux and run nats-server with `ants auth init` and `ants auth user alice --human` (ANTS_AUTH_DIR set), then:
1. Without systemd (`[boot] systemd=false` in /etc/wsl.conf, `wsl --shutdown`): `ants keys store alice.creds` must fail naming a missing D-Bus session bus, leaving the file as it was; `ants doctor` likewise.
2. With systemd (`[boot] systemd=true`, the default of recent Ubuntu images): install libsecret-tools, gnome-keyring and dbus-user-session; check `echo $DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` and that $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus exists; create and unlock the login keyring with `printf %s "$PW" | gnome-keyring-daemon --replace --unlock --components=secrets`.
3. Round trip: `ants keys store`, `secret-tool search service ants account KEY`, `ants doctor` (seed in the OS credential store), `ants keys unstore` (file byte-identical to the original), `ants keys store` again, `ants keys remove` (file and entry gone).
4. Locked case: store again, lock the keyring (`gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.secrets --object-path /org/freedesktop/secrets --method org.freedesktop.Secret.Service.Lock "[\"/org/freedesktop/secrets/collection/login\"]"`), then `ants doctor`, `ants keys unstore` and `ants keys remove` must fail as a locked store (not available yet) and keep the file; note whether a prompt appears (WSLg) and that a run without an answer fails after 60 s.
5. A systemd user service (the daemon unit of `scripts/install-units.sh`, its config naming an ant whose credentials seed is stored) reading a stored seed after `wsl --shutdown` and a new login, waiting while the keyring is locked and connecting once it is unlocked.
6. Confirm ants in WSL cannot reach the Windows Credential Manager, and that the README WSL bullet under "Private keys in the OS credential store" holds; correct it otherwise.
title: Verify the Secret Service key store on WSL 2

description: ants ask records the thread's owner in ants_owners directly through the hub's JetStream domain; when the leaf uplink is down the put fails with a warning while the message itself queues in ANTS_OUT, so ants' messages on that thread carry no owner and escalations go to the daemon's default human. description: A daemon down for more than 2 minutes after the outbox copy (or the watcher's letter) of a dead letter landed stores the letter again once it runs, on the redelivery or in the extra-delivery sweep (dead::finish), and the notice may come twice. Consider checking the hub's stream for an existing letter of the same stream sequence before storing.

A post by <from> to channel <channel> goes on 'ants.chan.<channel>.<from>', channel ids follow persona id syntax, stream ANTS stores ants.chan.>, and a reader drops a post whose 'from' or channel disagrees with its subject.
Channels do not replace thread notes (plan rooms): those stay passive boards that wake nobody.

A channel's members and optional messenger live in KV ants_channels under the channel id, written only by the human and read by personas; a member's daemon receives the channel's posts through its inbox consumer with the same ack, ordering, attempt and dead-letter guarantees as inbox messages, and a reader skips an entry whose channel disagrees with its key.

Each human channel post that mentions nobody prompts the channel's messenger, its assigned persona or else the default persona 'messenger', with triage rules ants adds to the prompt; it answers with a post on the same thread that @mentions the members relevant to it or says none are, and its mentions wake members only.

'ants channel create <channel>' with members and an optional messenger, and set/add/remove/list, manage channels; 'ants post #<channel> <text>' posts as the human, an @persona in the text wakes only that persona, '--thread' answers in a thread, and 'ants channel read <channel>' prints a channel's posts by thread.

comments.text: Evaluated on cargo 1.100 (fleet-30la, de7de1c). registry.global-min-publish-age (env CARGO_REGISTRY_GLOBAL_MIN_PUBLISH_AGE; values 'N days'/'N weeks'/'0'; resolver.incompatible-publish-age=deny by default) adopted at '7 days' in committed .cargo/config.toml. Findings: builds, cargo deny --locked, cargo install --path (uses Cargo.lock by default; reads repo config from crates/ants upward) all work with locked too-new versions. --git installs ignore repo config (discovery starts at CARGO_HOME) but also use the lock. cargo add picks cooldown-compliant versions (jiff 0.2.39 not 0.2.44). Friction: plain cargo update currently FAILS because manifests require uuid 1.29.2 (6 days old) and agent-client-protocol 5.2.0 (4 days); cargo update -p jiff DOWNGRADES locked 0.2.43 -> 0.2.39; --precise to a too-new version fails. Override: CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_PUBLISH_AGE=allow cargo update -p X --precise V. CI unaffected (no resolution; weekly deny uses lock). build.warnings: applies to clippy lints too and replays cached warnings without rebuild; set only in CI via CARGO_BUILD_WARNINGS=deny (workflow env), dropping '-- -D warnings'; not committed to config since it would make every local warning fatal and stop at the first warning crate. description: registry.global-min-publish-age (1.100) makes the resolver ignore crate versions newer than a set age unless already in Cargo.lock, complementing deny.toml. build.warnings = "deny" (1.97) can replace the -D warnings flag in .github/workflows/ci.yml. description: A channel is a named group of personas. A human post with no @mention is triaged by the messenger, which wakes only the members it judges relevant by @mentioning them in the channel. A post that @mentions personas wakes only them. Replies go back to the channel on the post's thread, like a Slack thread. Agent posts never fan out: they wake only the agents they @mention, spending turn budget.
design: Wire: stored subject ants.chan.<channel>.<from> in stream ANTS (outbox form ants.out.chan.<channel>.<from>). A post carries channel, thread id, from, text, explicit mentions (parsed from @persona tokens by the sender) and turn_budget. Membership: persona config channels = [...], published in the roster entry. The daemon adds ants.chan.<c>.* for each joined channel to its inbox consumer's filter subjects, so posts reuse ack-after-reply, per-thread ordering, attempts, dead letters and the leaf outbox; posts that do not mention the persona are acked unprompted. The messenger reads every channel and is prompted for each human post that mentions nobody; its answer is a post @mentioning the relevant members, or saying none are. A prompt on a channel thread includes the posts on that thread the persona has not seen. Distinct from plan rooms / thread notes (ants-9lvu), which stay passive.
title: Slack-style channels: fan-out posts with messenger triage and @mentions

description: Today the human is one identity, the persona 'human': agents escalate to it, only it holds the human rights, and the CLI always acts as it. Support several people, each with an own identity, inbox and credentials, all with the same rights. Waits for the channels epic (ants-367f), which also touches the wire contract and the human.
design:
Decisions (2026-11-14):
- Identity: a human is a persona listed in KV bucket ants_humans (key: persona id; value: HumanEntry naming that persona; a reader skips an entry whose persona disagrees with its key). Any name works, not only 'human'.
- Rights: all humans are equal; each has what 'human' has today (create/upgrade the stream and buckets, read/remove dead letters, send under any sender to replay, decide approvals, set up leaf outboxes and the intake, subscribe to ants.>). Rights come from the JWT: 'ants auth user NAME --human' issues them; without --human a persona's.
- Registry trust: only human credentials may write ants_humans; personas read it. The CLI registers its own human on connect. 'human' stays a human without an entry, so existing setups keep working.
- Escalation: an envelope carries 'owner', the human who started the thread; replies, send_message/ask_agent on the thread and threads an agent starts while handling it keep it. Turn budget spent, caps, dead-letter notices and plan rooms out of turns go to the owner; with no owner, to the daemon's configured default human (config 'human', default 'human').
- Approvals: any human decides; the first decision wins.
- Turn budget: a reply to any human spends none; a message from any human renews the thread's allowance. ants-proto stays I/O-free: the daemon tells it whether the sender is a human.

Spec changes to make with the work (bd spec change / add):
- wire ants-dnd.5, ants-dnd.6, ants-dnd.7; add: ants_humans registry; envelope owner.
- transport ants-h0k.7, ants-h0k.13, ants-h0k.14 ('the human' -> 'a human').
- daemon ants-0mi.9, ants-0mi.12; messenger ants-20j.2, ants-20j.4 ('the human' -> 'the thread's owner').
- cli ants-ved.6, ants-ved.7; add: the CLI acts as the human its credentials name.
- channels ants-2mfe.6, ants-2mfe.12, ants-2mfe.13 once channels land.
title: Several distinct humans on one team

comments.text: ants-xyb: a daemon's dead letter kept in the outbox and the copy its redelivery stores directly share Nats-Msg-Id dead-<stream seq>; landing more than two minutes apart (source retry backoff, 60 s ack wait), ANTS keeps both. Same remedy as for other late duplicates.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-83337b62
comments.text:
Investigation (nats-server v2.15.3, no code changed; issue left open).

LAG. ANTS (bus.rs:184 stream_config) sets no duplicate_window, so the server default of 2 min applies. The hub's ANTS_IN pulls each outbox through a source consumer. When the uplink drops, the source goes stale after 10 s and the hub sends a consumer-create request, waiting up to 30 s for a reply (srcConsumerWaitTime). After each failure it retries after 10 s x fails, capped at 2 min (stream.go calculateRetryBackoff). On leaf reconnect the hub restarts stale sources at once (leafnode.go checkInternalSyncConsumers -> retryDisconnectedSyncConsumers), except while a create request is still in flight (si.sip). In that case the retry waits for the 30 s timeout plus the backoff. The ANTS_IN -> ANTS hop is local and takes milliseconds. Worst-case landing after the uplink returns: about 30 + 120 + 2 = 152 s. Measured by instrumenting outbox.rs the_hub_takes_what_a_leaf_kept_while_its_uplink_was_down (reload-based outages, direct path back in 0.1 s): outages of 0/15/90/150/200/300 s landed 0.1-0.3 s after reconnect; 45 s -> 13 s; 60 s -> 48 s; 120 s -> 48 s; 240 s -> 79 s.

DUPLICATES. (a) bus::store_acked (bus.rs:471) falls back to the outbox on TimedOut (async-nats default 5 s). If the hub stored the message but the ack was lost, the outbox copy lands after the outage plus up to 152 s. That gap is unbounded by any window but is rare: it needs the uplink to fail between store and ack, or a hub slower than 5 s while the uplink is up, and in the second case the source is active and dedupes within milliseconds. (b) Dead letter (ants-xyb): a redelivery after reconnect calls bury_kept -> bury_letter. If the outbox copy has not landed yet, that path stores dead-<seq> directly, and the outbox copy can follow up to about 150 s later, past 2 min. That gives 2 letters, and replaying both delivers the message twice. Readers have no dedupe by envelope id: Answered notes (attempts.rs:121) live only until the ack, and the live Seen (bus.rs:537) holds only the last 1024 messages.

CONSEQUENCES of a late duplicate. An inbox message gets a second harness turn in the same session and a second reply; reply-<ant>-<id> no longer dedupes outside the window. A reply to ask_agent arriving late becomes a 'late replies' prompt. A channel post wakes or triages every member daemon again, which is the costliest case. Plan, notes and inbox listings show the message twice, and a human message renews the escalation allowance again.

REORDERING only spans the reconnect lag (0.1 s typical, about 150 s worst). A message sent directly after reconnect can be answered before an older buffered one on the same thread: the daemon queue keeps arrival order (daemon.rs ~480-510), inbox.rs:79 sorts by stream seq, and channel 'seen' uses seq watermarks, which stay safe because a late post counts as unseen. Nothing breaks, it is only out of order.

RECOMMENDATION:
(1) Set duplicate_window on ANTS explicitly to 24h. Add it to stream_config and let init_stream upgrade existing streams; ensure_stream warns like it does for other upgrades. Update the 'two minutes' wording in bus.rs:456-460, outbox.rs:16, dead.rs:23 and the README/docs. 5 min would already cover the dead-letter case and timeouts while the uplink is up. 24h also covers ack-lost cases across overnight outages. Cost: about 150 B of dedupe map per message id in the window (ddentry + map slot + id string), around 1.5 MB at 10k messages/day, plus a rebuildDedupe scan of one day's messages when the hub restarts. The server rejects only windows above max_age (30 d) or a server limit. Msg ids reused on purpose stay correct: replay-<seq>, mention.<post>.<human> and webhook hashes are meant to dedupe, and replays use a fresh id.
(2) Do not reorder by envelope sent_at in the daemon. Clocks differ between machines, it would mean holding messages back, and the lag is short. Optionally sort human-facing listings (inbox, plan, thread) by sent_at.
(3) Optional upstream: report the skipped reconnect kick while si.sip to nats-server.

description: Messages buffered across an outage land after what reached the hub meanwhile (source retry backoff up to ~2 min), and a timed-out direct publish that landed anyway duplicates once its buffered copy arrives after the 2-minute duplicate window. Measure in practice; consider a longer duplicate window on ANTS, or ordering by envelope timestamp in readers.
title: Bound reordering and late duplicates of buffered messages

comments.text: Correction: commits on fleet-ackv2 are 8a310cb (grants, test-support flag), dbf2afb (docs, CI, observer helper) and merges 20a450b, 3e05dce.

description:
nats-server 2.16 turns on feature flag js_ack_fc_v2 by default. Ack and flow-control reply subjects then change from $JS.ACK.<stream>.<consumer>.... to $JS.ACK.<domain>.<account hash>.<stream>.<consumer>.... (ADR-15; https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.14#domain-aware-acknowledgement-and-flow-control-subjects). The same goes for $JS.FC. ants-proto Permissions grant only the v1 form: $JS.ACK.ANTS.<consumer>.> and $JS.FC.<stream>.> (crates/ants-proto/src/lib.rs about lines 939-1218: inbox, chan, notify consumers, KV watchers, outbox). On such a hub every ack an ant or human sends is denied, so messages are redelivered until they become dead letters, and KV watches stall on flow control.

Reproduced on nats-server 2.15.3 by adding `feature_flags { js_ack_fc_v2: true }` to the test servers in ants-test-support: 5 tests in crates/ants fail with "double ack response timed out": credentials_confine_each_user_to_its_role, clients_on_a_leaf_node_reach_the_hub_stream_through_its_domain, ants_post_to_channels_as_themselves_and_read_but_never_write_the_channels_bucket, failed_messages_become_dead_letters_the_human_replays and the_read_state_of_the_old_inbox_consumer_moves_into_the_marker. All 5 pass without the flag.

Fix: grant both forms, e.g. $JS.ACK.*.*.ANTS.<consumer>.> beside the v1 subject. Check which domain token a hub without a domain uses. Bump PERMISSIONS_VERSION so that ants doctor and creds checks flag old credentials for renewal. Run CI with the flag on, for at least the auth tests. Document in README and docs/transport.md that credentials must be renewed before the hub upgrades to 2.16.
title: Allow v2 JetStream ack and flow-control subjects in credentials before hubs move to nats-server 2.16

description:
One human can use several devices today (ants auth user NAME --human issues a new key per run; earlier creds stay valid), but all share the durable pull consumer inbox-<name>: a reply read on one device is acked and never reaches the others, two ants inbox -f sessions split replies between them, and messages peeked on one device stay hidden from the others for ACK_WAIT (60s).

Wanted: every device of a human sees every reply. Live delivery fans out to all connected devices (e.g. core subscription on the stored-inbox republish, or an ordered consumer per device); read state is per human and synced (a read marker in KV that every device honours and updates), so reading on one device marks read everywhere without consuming the message for the others. Keep ack-after-store semantics and ants ask --wait / --follow behaviour.

Device identity: each device gets a unique generated ID (not chosen by the human, never reused; e.g. UUIDv7 or derived from the device's user NKey) plus a human-readable label (e.g. 'Quang's iPhone', editable, need not be unique). The ID is carried in the device's user JWT and keys per-device state (consumer, presence, push target); the label is for display in a device listing (e.g. ants auth devices NAME) and for picking a device to rename or revoke (ants-4zlw), with the ID disambiguating duplicate labels.
title: Multi-device humans: every device receives every reply, with read state synced across devices

description: ACP clients for agent harnesses.
title: Agent harnesses
Copilot CLI is driven over ACP with 'copilot --acp' on stdio.
By default tool requests are rejected; requests outside the persona's allowlist go to ants.approvals.<persona> and to every persona of its escalate_to, and are rejected on timeout.

Each ant may configure a model, reasoning effort and provider-native context tier or window; the daemon applies explicit settings before prompting new and resumed sessions, verifies settings returned through ACP selectors, fails unsupported settings without silent fallback, and preserves harness defaults when settings are omitted.
By default tool requests are rejected; requests outside the ant's allowlist go to ants.approvals.<ant> and to every ant of its escalate_to, and are rejected on timeout.
An ant's harness is its own harness key, else the config file's top-level harness, else copilot; the top-level harness also runs the built-in messenger, and a top-level provider key fails to load.
Copilot CLI is a built-in harness definition run as 'copilot --acp' on stdio.
Claude Code is a built-in harness definition run through its ACP adapter 'claude-agent-acp'; other ACP agents and adapters, such as Codex's, are added through configuration without rebuilding ants.
Google Antigravity CLI is a built-in harness definition run as 'agy acp --disable-telemetry' on stdio.

Harness sessions run in a mode that sends tool requests to the client: a harness definition may name the ACP session mode every new and resumed session is switched to, the built-in Claude Code and Antigravity CLI definitions name 'default', and a harness that lacks its named mode fails the session.

An ant's harness is its own harness key, else the config file's top-level harness, else copilot, each resolved by name through the harness registry; the top-level harness also runs the built-in messenger, and a top-level provider key fails to load.

Harnesses are named definitions in a registry, the built-in ones and the config file's [harnesses.<name>] tables, each an executable, an argument list, environment overrides, an optional session mode and the context values it takes; a file definition replaces a built-in of the same name whole, and every harness runs as executable plus arguments without a shell.
Permission requests are answered by option kind, never by position or label.
A harness reference with no definition, a definition with an invalid name, an empty command or an unknown key fails when the config file loads.

A harness process gets the daemon's environment, the definition's env over it and the ant's env over both; a command with a path separator resolves like other config paths, and a bare name is looked up on PATH at launch.

A harness definition's context values select launch arguments, a model ID suffix, or both; a value with a suffix requires an explicit model, and a harness without context values rejects an ant's context.

A harness definition may name the command that signs the harness in (sign_in); a harness is signed out when session/new, session/load or a prompt fails with ACP auth_required (-32000) or with error or stderr text that unambiguously says it is not signed in, and its sign-in command is the definition's, else the terminal auth method its initialize response offers.

A reusable handshake check starts a harness, completes initialize and session/new without MCP servers, stops it and reports it ready (with the agent it names), missing (executable not at its path or on PATH), signed out or failed, together with its sign-in command; ants harness check runs it.

A harness error reporting a provider limit is classified, after sign-in, as a rate limit (HTTP 429 or 529 after a status word, common phrases such as too many requests or overloaded, or the definition's rate_limited phrases) or an exhausted quota (common phrases such as quota exceeded or usage limit, or the definition's quota_exhausted phrases), a wait the error names being read as a hint capped at 7 days.

A harness prompt error saying the session outgrew the model's context window is classified as a context overflow by common phrases, such as context_length_exceeded, maximum context length or prompt is too long, or by the definition's context_overflow phrases, matched case-insensitively; a blank phrase fails the config file.
On Windows a bare harness command is looked up on PATH as an .exe, .cmd or .bat file, in that order, and the file found is started, so harnesses installed by npm as .cmd scripts start.

A harness error reporting a provider limit is classified, after sign-in, as a rate limit (HTTP 429 or 529 after a status word, phrases such as overloaded, or the definition's rate_limited phrases) or an exhausted quota (phrases such as quota exceeded, or the definition's quota_exhausted phrases), a named wait read as a hint capped at 7 days; a reply made only of short Error:, API Error:, Info: or ⚠ lines is read as such an error and, if it reports a limit, not sent.

The *.toml files of harnesses.d beside the config file, in name order and hidden ones skipped, hold [harnesses.<name>] tables alone, a relative command resolved against harnesses.d; a name defined twice across them and the config file fails naming both files, an unknown key fails naming its file, and their changes reload the daemon.
By default tool requests are rejected; requests outside the persona's allowlist go to ants.approvals.<persona> and are rejected on timeout.

Harnesses are named definitions in a registry, the built-in ones, the config file's [harnesses.<name>] tables and those of its harnesses.d drop-in files, each an executable, an argument list, environment overrides, an optional session mode and the context values it takes; a file definition replaces a built-in of the same name whole, and every harness runs as executable plus arguments without a shell.

By default tool requests are rejected; requests outside the ant's allowlist, or outside the narrowed tool rules of the thread they are made on, go to ants.approvals.<ant> and to every ant of its escalate_to, and are rejected on timeout.
Claude Code and Codex are supported through their ACP adapters.

description:
Headless agent teams on several machines talk to each other and to the human from a terminal, without SSH or inbound public ports.

Decided:
- Backbone: NATS + JetStream (durable inboxes, acks, redelivery) and NATS KV (roster, sessions). Replaces Buzz's relay.
- Transport is pluggable: Dev Tunnels (TCP), direct ws/wss, or an HTTPS fallback bridge. Agents always talk to a local NATS leaf node; only the leaf's uplink changes.
- Persona daemon (antsd) per machine drives agent harnesses over ACP (stdio JSON-RPC). Copilot CLI (copilot --acp) first.
- Memory efficiency: Rust, one 'ants' binary (CLI, daemon, MCP), tokio current-thread, harness processes capped and evicted when idle.
- Names: project ants; subjects under ants.; stream ANTS; KV ants_roster, ants_sessions.
Source: 'Headless Agent Communication Over Dev Tunnels' design discussion.
title: Architecture: NATS/JetStream backbone, persona daemon, ACP harnesses, Rust

A post by <from> to the plan room of thread <thread> goes on 'ants.plan.<thread>.<from>', and a reader drops a post whose 'from' or thread disagrees with its subject.
A roster entry belongs to the persona of its KV key, and a reader skips an entry whose 'persona' disagrees with its key.

description: In crates/ants/src/enroll.rs `request`, the repeat-tick arm of the select! awaits `client.publish(...)` and `client.flush()`. When the enrollment JWT expires the server disconnects the client before the local `expiry` sleep fires (the sleep ends at exp plus the fraction of the current second). async-nats 0.52 then retries the reconnect forever (no max_reconnects) with the expired credentials, and a pending flush is answered only after a reconnect, so `flush()` never returns. While the arm is stuck, neither `expiry` nor `stop` (Ctrl-C) can win, so `ants` hangs instead of reporting the expiry. Seen as a hang of about 9 hours in the test `enroll::tests::a_rejection_or_the_expiry_ends_the_request` (its last `request` call has no timeout) during a full `cargo test` run with ANTS_TEST_JS_ACK_FC_V2=1. It is intermittent: 6 reruns passed. Fix: bound the flush (e.g. timeout of `repeat`) or race it against expiry/stop, and stop on an expired-authentication server error. Also give the test a timeout.
title: enroll::request can hang forever once its enrollment credentials expire

title: On Linux the OS credential store is the Secret Service through secret-tool, the seed on its standard input and each call bounded by 60 s; a locked keyring, which secret-tool reports as nothing found, is told from a missing entry by a locked collection listing no entries over D-Bus or a search listing locked entries, so reading or deleting a locked entry fails as a store not available yet, never as missing or deleted; errors name what is missing (secret-tool, D-Bus, Secret Service, keyring).

No ant's or webhook's credentials list the keys of ants_sessions, ants_attempts or ants_owners: an ant reads and writes only its own keys of the first two, reading by key also every ant's daily spend key for pool caps, and ants read and webhooks record owners by key, all without stream info of those buckets, which only a human's credentials get, to create them and find spend keys; a human reads by key only the thread and daily spend keys of ants_sessions.

Observer credentials ('ants auth user NAME --observer') publish only their renewal request and JetStream requests on their own ANTS consumers 'observe-requests|decisions|dead-<observer>' (filters ants.approvals.*, ants.approvals.*.* and ants.dead.> pinned in the create subject) and reads and watches of ants_roster; they subscribe only to those subjects, ants.status.*.* and their reply inboxes, reading no inbox, notes, channel, other bucket or stream info.

A manager ant's request for a new ant travels on core NATS `ants.antreq.<manager>`, signed by the manager's credentials and answered on `ants.antreq.<manager>.reply`, through leaf uplinks too, whose credentials the signer renews to carry the new ant; added to permissions version 4.

Credentials that ack JetStream messages or answer flow control allow both subject forms: v1 '$JS.ACK.<stream>.<consumer>.>' and '$JS.FC.<stream>.>', and v2 (nats-server 2.16's default, js_ack_fc_v2) '$JS.ACK.*.*.<stream>.<consumer>.>' and '$JS.FC.<domain>.*.<stream>.>' (domain '*', or the machine's for a leaf's outbox), never '$JS.ACK.>' or '$JS.FC.>'; those older than permissions version 4 must be renewed before the hub or a leaf node moves to 2.16.

'ants auth leaf', the approval of an enrollment through a leaf node and 'ants signer' for a manager's request through one refuse uplink credentials whose JWT exceeds 16 times server.conf's max_control_line less 4 KiB, naming their size and the limit, before writing, admitting, signing or answering anything, the signer before asking any human; uplink permissions stay those of each user on the machine, never widened to patterns to save space.

After writing leaf uplink credentials that request_ant renewed, the manager's daemon, before listing the new ant, rewrites the remote's credentials path in leaf.conf to another spelling of the same file and reloads the leaf node service running it, so nats-server 2.14 or later reconnects the uplink alone with the renewed credentials while local connections stay up; otherwise its answer names the reload to run.

'ants signer' answers a manager's retire request on ants.antreq.<manager>, signed apart from an addition, by revoking the ant's key and the keys of the name issued before it only when issued.jsonl records them as added from a template by that manager, then pushing the account to the hub, so the ant no longer counts toward max_ants; otherwise it refuses and revokes nothing.

Credentials let every user put, delete and direct-get only its own reaction keys ($KV.ants_reactions.<self>.>), so nobody can react as another or remove another's reaction; humans also create KV_ants_reactions and read all of it by stream info, direct gets and ordered consumers; ants, observers, webhooks and the channel manager read no one else's reactions; these rights are part of permissions version 4.
A persona reads plan rooms back from the stream only through its own consumer 'plan-<persona>', which filters plan subjects only.

A human's credentials may create ants_threads, get its stream info, and put and direct-get every title.* key but only its own marks.<human> key, so no human reads or changes another's pins and archives; ants, observers, webhooks and the channel manager get no right on the bucket, and a hub without it or human credentials without these rights make ants thread list warn and the commands needing it fail naming the fix.

Within permissions version 4 humans publish ants.queue.* and create and direct-get only $KV.ants_attempts.*.msg.* marks, while an ant hears only ants.queue.<self> and answers only on ants.queued.<self>.

'ants auth backup FILE' writes the team's operator, account and system account seeds, server.conf, issued.jsonl and revoked.json to FILE, mode 0600, encrypted with a non-empty passphrase (from --passphrase-file, ANTS_BACKUP_PASSPHRASE or the terminal without echo) in the age v1 scrypt format; 'ants auth restore FILE' writes them back as files of the team directory, refusing existing team files without --force, and a wrong passphrase or an altered file restores nothing.

Permissions version 4 lets every user list the streams ($JS.API.STREAM.LIST, which carries sizes and no subject stored) and every ant read the account's JetStream info ($JS.API.INFO) and create, direct-get and delete the storage warning notes $KV.ants_sessions._storage.*.*.warned, and no other key of another ant.
Every ants process on a machine connects to its local NATS leaf node; switching the uplink to the hub changes leaf configuration only.

Live waiters for a user's messages (ants ask --wait, a waiting ask_ant, an ant waiting on its escalation chain) get each inbox message once, published directly or taken by the hub from a leaf's outbox: the hub's ANTS stream republishes each stored inbox message to '_INBOX.<recipient>.stored.<sender>', which only the recipient (and its leaf's uplink) may read and none may publish to; waiters take only those with no reply subject and single Nats-Stream (ANTS) and Nats-Subject (inbox) headers.

description: Found by a security audit. bus::as_published (crates/ants-daemon/src/bus.rs) takes the first Nats-Subject header of a message on _INBOX.<user>.stored.* and makes it the message's subject; callers then run Envelope::check_subject against that attacker-writable text, so any 'from' passes. The server publishes there on behalf of any client: a direct get answers on any reply subject with the stored headers before its own (an ant may put its roster key with a forged Nats-Subject and direct-get it to _INBOX.<human>.stored.<x>), a push consumer delivers to any deliver subject, and the hub's republish appends its own Nats-Subject after one a publisher wrote (directly or through a leaf's outbox). An ant that knows a thread id can thus make ants ask --wait/--follow show a reply from another ant or human; the daemon's live inbox (ask_agent replies, chain approval decisions) takes the same path. Fix: take a message there only as the ANTS stream republished it: no reply subject, the subject _INBOX.<user>.stored.<from>, exactly one Nats-Stream (ANTS) and exactly one Nats-Subject (ants.inbox.<user>.<from>). Test against nats-server; correct the trust statement in ants-proto and the transport requirement ants-h0k.40.
title: Waiters trust a forged Nats-Subject header on _INBOX.<user>.stored.*, so any ant can spoof a reply's sender

description:
Proposal (needs the owner's decision, a behaviour change via bd spec change of the worktrees requirement ants-0mi.56): when an ant's config leaves worktrees unset, turn it on for a workdir inside a git work tree with max_harnesses above 1, keeping worktrees = false as an explicit opt-out. Today such ants only get a warning (ants-ag81).
Trade-offs:
- Disk use: one full checkout per thread under <home>/worktrees, plus build outputs (target/, node_modules) each thread builds from scratch; large repos multiply that by up to max_harnesses live threads and by every thread whose session has not expired yet.
- Branch clutter: a branch ants/<ant>/<thread> per thread in the user's repository; branches with unmerged commits are kept after their worktree is removed and need merging or deleting by hand.
- Harness behaviour: worktrees start from HEAD without uncommitted changes in the workdir, so a thread does not see work in progress there; edits land on the thread's branch, not in the workdir the user looks at, until merged; tools or harness settings keyed by the workdir path (trust prompts, per-directory config, caches) see a new directory per thread.
- Config shape: worktrees would become Option<bool> so an explicit false stays distinguishable from unset; config::to_table and the README config example change accordingly.
title: Default worktrees on for git workdirs of ants with concurrent threads

Vocabulary: a token with the user-id syntax (1-64 of a-z 0-9 '-', starting with a letter or digit), so it is a valid subject/KV token; docs suggest eyes, check, thumbsup, x, heart, rocket. Storage: KV bucket ants_reactions, key <reactor>.<message-id>.<reaction>, value JSON {message, by, reaction, at}; readers take the reactor from the key and skip a body disagreeing with it. Add = put (idempotent); remove = delete marker on one's own key, a no-op when absent. Bucket: max_age 30 days like the ANTS stream, one value per key, deny_delete/deny_purge and no rollup so no one can wipe the bucket. Authorization: reactor-first keys let credentials grant put/delete/direct-get of $KV.ants_reactions.<self>.> only, so forging or removing another's reaction is denied; a human's devices share the human key. Humans read the whole bucket (they read all threads already); ants write their own only and cannot read others'; observers, webhooks and channel managers get nothing. Gap: subjects cannot tie an opaque message id to access to that message, so an ant can react under any id; harmless since only humans read reactions. No outbox form behind a leaf: reacting needs the hub. Folded into PERMISSIONS_VERSION 4. description: Each persona may name agents to escalate to. The first is the leader. The group tries to resolve the issue; when it cannot, the leader escalates up its own chain, until a persona with no chain hands it to the thread's owner (a human, ants-548b).
design:
Decisions (2026-11-14):
- Config: persona key escalate_to = [leader, member, ...], optional; the first entry leads. Published in the roster entry, so any daemon can follow a chain past an offline leader.
- Triggers: everything that goes to the human today (turn budget spent, caps reached, plan room out of turns, dead-letter notices, tool approvals) goes to the persona's chain first; plus an MCP tool escalate(issue) an agent calls when stuck.
- Group: fan-out. Every member gets the escalation; they coordinate in the thread's plan room; only the leader resolves (answers the stuck agent on its thread) or escalates further (escalate tool, or automatically when the group spends its budget or caps).
- Loops: the escalation records the personas it went through and its level; a target already visited, or more than max_escalation_hops (default 3), goes straight to the owner.
- Budget: a resolution from an agent gives the stuck thread a fresh turn budget and allowance at most once per chain level; the next spend escalates one level higher. Only a human resets the level. The level lives with the thread's spend in ants_sessions so restarts keep it.
- Offline: targets are not skipped; JetStream holds the escalation. With no resolution within escalate_after (config), the escalating daemon escalates one level higher (the leader's chain from the roster).
- Approvals: tool requests go up the chain too. An agent's decision travels as a message from a persona in the requester's escalate_to; the requesting daemon accepts decisions only from its own chain (sender pinned by subject), so persona credentials need no rights on ants.approvals.<other>.*. Humans can still decide directly; the first decision wins.
- Visibility: ants watch and the roster show escalations and chains.
