comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-63a6cadf
comments.text:
Hand-off from .1/.4 (branch fleet-templates, commits d5b7b92, e9b9df7).

DATA MODEL. crates/ants-daemon/src/template.rs: AntTemplate (from [[ant_template]], deny_unknown_fields): name, managers (exact ant names, empty = nobody), name (glob, '<manager>' placeholder, e.g. '<manager>-*'), harnesses, models (model ID -> highest Effort; Effort low<medium<high<xhigh<max), contexts, allow (fixed rules), allow_sets (name -> rules), ceilings max_thread_cost/tokens, max_daily_cost/tokens, max_harnesses, prompt_timeout, max_tool_calls (template value is both default and ceiling; 0 = unlimited only if the template is 0), max_ants, pool_daily_cost/tokens, plus fixed env, worktrees, idle_timeout, approval_timeout, spend_warn_percent. A templated [[ant]] carries only TEMPLATED_KEYS (name, template, added_by, creds, nats, js_domain) + template::REQUEST_KEYS; any other key -> 'ant X: KEY comes from template T'. Resolved ant: escalate_to=[manager], allow_tools=false, allow = template allow + chosen sets. Checked at load and on reload (config::check_added: max_ants, an added ant is never a manager, pool membership).

CHECK API (call from request_ant .2 and the approval signer .3):
- Loaded::check_request(&self, manager, name, template, &Request) -> Result<Ant>: template exists, manager listed in managers and not itself added, name free (no ant/schedule), name fits pattern, count < max_ants, then AntTemplate::resolve. Resolves ~/relative workdir against the config dir.
- AntTemplate::resolve(manager, name, &Request) -> Result<Ant>; errors name the violated bound.
- template::Request: serde deny_unknown_fields, so it deserializes from JSON too (prompt_timeout is a duration string like '10m').
- config::template_entry(name, template, manager, creds: Option<&Path>, &Request) -> Result<String> renders the minimal [[ant]] TOML; config::append re-parses the whole file, so the write is re-checked.

POOL (.4): caps::Pool {template, daily_cost, daily_tokens, members: Members(Arc<RwLock<Vec<UserId>>>)} on daemon::Config.pool; Ledger::with_pool. Total = sum of every member's <ant>.day.<today> in ants_sessions (own day from memory); read errors warn and fail open. Pool warning once/day via DaySpend.pool_warned. Members compares equal always; serve::reconcile replaces members in place on reload. Ant creds may direct-get $KV.ants_sessions.*.day.* (PERMISSIONS_VERSION 4).

NOTES/RISKS for .2/.3/.5/.6: approval 'always allow' (with_allow_rule) on a templated ant would add an allow key, which the load refuses — .3 must handle it. Retiring an ant (.5) drops its spend from the pool total for the rest of the day. Membership is per config file (same template name in two files = two pools). check_request's 'manager is an added ant' only sees the same file. The load check does not require added_by to still be in managers (removing a manager keeps its workers). Pre-v4 creds or leaf uplinks: pool reads denied -> warning per prompt, cap not enforced.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-4b4c5501
comments.text:
Hand-off after ants-o6t7.3, ants-o6t7.2 and ants-m3k0 (branch fleet-templates2: 5a16cfe, 342490c, 2c85861, e840e7c, 943aca1).

What exists:
- Wire (ants-proto): AntRequest/AntReply on core NATS ants.antreq.<manager> / .reply (subject::antreq, antreq_reply, ALL_ANT_REQUESTS, ALL_ANT_REPLIES); ants publish antreq(self), subscribe antreq_reply(self); Permissions::for_enroll_approver hears all requests, answers, files approvals and direct-gets their decisions. All in PERMISSIONS_VERSION 4.
- Signer (crates/ants/src/signer.rs): serve() judges by config::signer_templates(--config) and Loaded-free template::check/resolve_with; counts max_ants via live(dir) = issued.jsonl records neither revoked nor expired with Issued.template == T (revoke.rs Issued.template/added_by, written by auth::sign_added). Outside policy: ApprovalRequest of the manager (kind other, title 'request_ant: add ant N from template T (why)', AllowOnce/Reject), decisions via direct_get_last_for_subject. Behind a leaf: auth::extend_leaf + members::enrolled + outbox::admit_ant. Client side: signer::ask(client, jwt, key, template, request_json, reason, thread, name, user_key, leaf, repeat, until) -> Signed{jwt, leaf_jwt}.
- Daemon side (ants-daemon mcp.rs): AntAsk, AntRequester (Arc<dyn Fn(AntAsk)->BoxFuture<Result<String,String>>>), Requester (PartialEq by presence, so reconcile does not restart managers), Mcp::with_requester, daemon::Config.requester; the tool route is removed when no requester is set. main.rs sets it for serve::Listed.managers (only when the whole file is served; manager::manages(templates, ant, added) excludes added ants).
- Requester (crates/ants/src/manager.rs): Manager::add takes a process-global lock, config::load + Loaded::check_request, refuses if <keys>/<name>.creds exists, reuses/creates <name>.nk (add::seed_path), signer::ask, auth::write_creds, removes the seed, add::renew_uplink (no leaf restart: the answer names the restart), config::append(config::template_entry(...)); the reload (reload::CHECK_EVERY polling) serves the ant; Hub::request_ant waits up to 60 s for the roster entry.
- Test: manager::tests::a_manager_adds_ants_that_its_daemon_serves_after_the_reload runs signer + serve::run + Manager in-process against a real nats-server.

For ants-o6t7.5 (retire_ant): mirror request_ant with a second requester (or widen AntRequester to an enum of asks) set the same way for managers; check added_by == caller in the local file. Stopping = remove the [[ant]] entry (config edit like tools.rs --rule uses toml_edit; reload stops it as on Ctrl-C). Revocation needs the account key: add an AntRequest-like 'retire' message for ants signer (it should verify added_by == manager from its issued.jsonl, then revoke::revoke the ant's keys and push the account, as ants auth revoke does); once revoked, live() stops counting it toward max_ants and the 'name held by another live key' refusal clears, so a later request_ant of the same name works. Keep the home (~/.ants/<name>, from config) but move/delete <keys>/<name>.creds, since Manager::add refuses a name whose .creds exists. A human CLI (e.g. ants retire NAME) can run the same steps locally plus ants auth revoke.

For ants-o6t7.6 (leaf growth/restarts): the signer's signed() calls auth::extend_leaf, which already refuses past the 252 KiB uplink limit (the request is refused with that reason, nothing admitted). Manager::add writes the renewed uplink with add::renew_uplink but never restarts the leaf node (service::manual(Service::Nats, Action::Restart) is only named in the answer); batching restarts or pre-provisioning room per template's max_ants would go in signer::signed (pre-provision) and manager.rs (restart policy). The leaf's members bookkeeping is members::enrolled.

description:
A manager ant designs work with architect ants, then adds as many worker ants as the work needs instead of a human pre-creating them on a VM. Ants beat bare harness sessions here: each keeps its own memory and task tracking and can grow into a subject-matter expert across work. Parallelism alone does not need new ants (max_harnesses threads, worktrees = true); this is for distinct, lasting roles.

Safety rests on ant templates ([[ant_template]] in config) a human writes: a manager can never widen what a template allows, approval follows a policy (quota, names) or falls back to a human, total spend is bounded per template, and added ants can be retired.
title: Let a manager ant add worker ants from human-defined ant templates

close_reason: Done in d5b7b92 (fleet-templates): [[ant_template]] (crates/ants-daemon/src/template.rs) with allowlists, ceilings, allow sets, max_ants, managers and name pattern; templated [[ant]] entries checked at load and reload; Loaded::check_request / AntTemplate::resolve / config::template_entry as the reusable check. Specs ants-0mi.88, ants-0mi.89.
description:
An [[ant_template]] entry, written by a human, bounds every ant added from it:
- harnesses: allowlist.
- models: explicit allowlist mapping each model ID to its highest reasoning effort (model IDs are opaque per harness, so no 'below model X' ordering; an unlisted or new model is refused). Effort ranked low < medium < high < xhigh < max; an effort outside that list or above the model's ceiling is refused.
- contexts: allowlist (1m costs more, so opt-in).
- ceilings for max_thread_cost/tokens, max_daily_cost/tokens, max_harnesses, prompt_timeout, max_tool_calls: a request may ask for less, never more.
- allow rules fixed by the template, or chosen from named sets it defines (glob-subset checks are not attempted).
- max_ants and pool_daily_cost (see pool spend task); managers: the ants allowed to use it, by exact name, none by default (an ant not listed in any template cannot add ants); name pattern (e.g. <manager>-*).
Unknown keys fail config loading, as for [[ant]].

Added ants can never add ants themselves, whatever templates say: a manager is listed by a human, not by another ant, so no chain of ants adding ants grows past one level.
Each [[ant]] added from it records template = "<name>" and added_by = "<manager>"; its other settings come from the ant template, so a reload re-checks it against the current [[ant_template]].
title: Config [[ant_template]]: allowlists and ceilings for ants a manager adds

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-805df714
comments.text: Decision for leaf uplink growth with request_ant (commit 23ff8a6 on fleet-leafgrow): (1) No pre-provisioning: NATS wildcards match whole tokens and an ant name is one token, so '<manager>-*' cannot be written, '*' would let the leaf carry any ant, and hub stream interest crosses only with literal anchors; names come per request. Per-ant growth stays, measured by auth test each_ant_added_grows_the_uplink_by_the_same_measure: ~4.2 KB/ant, ~8.0 KB with a JS domain (docs now say about 30 ants per leaf with a domain, 60 without). (2) Refuse past the limit early: Signer::judge checks extend_leaf before live()/policy, so the request is refused at once with 'the uplink of the leaf node M cannot carry N: ... would take ... another leaf node', no human asked; Signer::signed renews the uplink before sign_added, so nothing is recorded for a refused ant (sign_added used to record first). Test an_ant_the_uplink_has_no_room_for_is_refused_before_a_human_is_asked. (3) No leaf restart, no batching needed: Manager::add, after renew_uplink, calls leaf::reconnect_uplink: toggles './' before the credentials file name in leaf.conf and reloads the leaf service (SIGHUP). nats-server 2.14+ identifies a remote by urls+account+credentials path, so the reload drops/re-adds that remote alone; the uplink reconnects with the renewed JWT, local connections stay up. Done before config::append so the ant's first connection finds the uplink. description: Webhook ingress: events from outside services delivered to an ant or a channel.
title: Webhook ingress

'ants webhook serve' takes 'POST <path>/<webhook>' for each [[webhook]] of its config file (default ~/.ants/webhooks.toml) and delivers each event, as that webhook, only to its configured ant's inbox or channel, on a new thread owned by the human its config names, if any; the sender cannot choose the destination.

With public_url and an action secret, an approval notice carries one link per offered verdict, signed with HMAC-SHA256 over the ant, request id, stream sequence, verdict, human and the request's expiry; GET on '<path>/_approval' only shows the request and a confirm button, and POST stores the ApprovalDecision with the human's credentials as 'ants tools approve' does, refusing a wrong signature (403), an expired link (410) or an answered request (409).
A human's credentials may create, read and ack only its own notification consumer 'notify-<human>' on ANTS; other users' credentials cannot create it.

A [[human.notify]] sink with 'device' gets no notice while that device follows what the notice is about (tool requests for approvals, the inbox for escalations), while the human's other sinks still get it; a sink without 'device' gets every notice, unreadable presence counts as away, and 'ants webhook serve' refuses device sinks for credentials without presence rights.

'ants webhook serve' reloads its config file on SIGHUP and once the file changed on disk and stayed unchanged across two checks (every 3 s): webhooks and humans newly listed start, those no longer listed stop, those whose entry or credentials file changed (all of them for another hub or domain, humans for other links) start again, and the others and the HTTP listener carry on; a file that fails to load is logged and the config served stays.

'ants webhook notify-test HUMAN' sends a test notice through each ntfy, Slack or Telegram sink of that human in the webhooks' config file, prints one line per sink (ok, or the failure: HTTP status or error, without URL or token), and exits non-zero when one fails.

A webhook request is authenticated, by an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body (hex, with or without a sha256= prefix, in its configured header), a bearer token, or a token alone in a configured header (auth = "token"), compared in constant time, before anything is read from or stored on NATS; a failure answers 401 and stores nothing.

'ants webhook add NAME (--to ANT | --channel CH) [--preset github|gitlab|grafana]' refuses a name already listed, issues the webhook's credentials with the account key (or with --enroll asks over NATS for 'ants enroll approve NAME --webhook', which refuses a request through a leaf node), writes a new random secret to a 0600 file beside the config file, appends the [[webhook]] entry keeping the file's text, reloads the webhook service and prints the URL and secret.

The presets of 'ants webhook add' match what each sender sends: github hmac-sha256 in X-Hub-Signature-256 with id header:X-GitHub-Delivery; gitlab auth token in X-Gitlab-Token with id header:Idempotency-Key; grafana hmac-sha256 in X-Grafana-Alerting-Signature (no timestamp header) with id body-sha256; none, a bearer token with the default id and text.

'ants webhook serve' notifies each [[human]] of its config of pending tool requests and of escalations reaching its inbox through its ntfy, Slack, Telegram, exec or http sinks, reading as that human its durable consumer 'notify-<human>' so several processes send each event once; requests already decided or expired are skipped, and a failing sink is logged without its URL, token, secret or command arguments and never stops the others.

'ants webhook notify-test HUMAN' sends a test notice through each sink of that human in the webhooks' config file, whatever its kind (ntfy, slack, telegram, exec, http), prints one line per sink (ok, or the failure: HTTP status, exit status or error, without URL, token or command arguments), and exits non-zero when one fails.

A webhook request is authenticated, by an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body or a bearer token compared in constant time, before anything is read from or stored on NATS; a failure answers 401 and stores nothing.

An exec or http sink gets each notice as one JSON object of version 1: kind (approval, escalation or test), id, human, title, text, urgent, sent_at and links (one per offered verdict with public_url), plus ant, thread, request, seq, tool, options and expires_at for an approval and ant, thread, reason, stuck and level for an escalation; later versions only add fields, and a breaking change raises version.

An exec sink runs its command (program and arguments, no shell) with the JSON notice as one line on standard input, and fails when the command exits non-zero or outlives the sink's timeout (default 10 s, 1 s to 30 s), which kills and reaps it.

An http sink POSTs the JSON notice with X-Ants-Timestamp (Unix seconds) and X-Ants-Signature 'sha256=' and the lowercase hex HMAC-SHA256, keyed with its secret (secret_file of mode 0600 or secret_env, 16+ characters), of the timestamp, a '.' and the raw body; any answer but 2xx fails it.
'ants doctor' fails an exec sink whose program path is no executable file and warns of a bare program name not on its PATH.

Every [[human.notify]] sink kind goes through one dispatch path: one notice model formatted per kind, the device-presence filter, all sinks at once each within its timeout, and failures logged by sink label only; existing ntfy, Slack and Telegram entries keep working and sending what they sent.

A [[human]] entry's quiet = 'HH:MM-HH:MM' holds back its notices within that window on the wall clock of the entry's timezone, else the webhook file's top-level timezone, else UTC, daylight saving time included; a start after the end crosses midnight, the start is inside and the end outside; a malformed window, one starting where it ends, an unknown zone or a timezone without quiet fails loading the file.

ants webhook serve holds back a notice whose thread the human muted, whatever its kind, and, while the human is snoozed or within quiet hours, every notice but the kinds the entry's bypass lists (approvals, escalations; default none); test notices are never held back.
A held-back notice is dropped and logged, never sent later, and marks nothing read and decides nothing: its tool request stays pending and its message unread.

With completions = true (default false) on a [[human]] entry, a reply reaching the human's inbox (in_reply_to set; no escalation, approval, mention or webhook message) is pushed as a notice of kind completion naming the replying ant and the thread, once per message across all ants webhook serve instances sharing the notify-<human> consumer.

Each human's snooze deadline and muted threads with their deadlines are one JSON key <human> in KV ants_notify (file, no TTL, created like the other buckets), which only that human puts and direct-gets; a hold ends at its stored deadline without being lifted, and ants webhook serve reads the key by direct get per notice, holding nothing back by it when it is missing, malformed or unreadable, or, with a warning naming the renewal, when the credentials lack its rights.

A webhook's credentials publish only 'ants.inbox.<ant>.<webhook>' and 'ants.chan.<channel>.<webhook>' for their destinations and the webhook's own keys in ants_webhooks, read only those keys and the entries of their channels, subscribe only the webhook's reply inboxes, and write neither ants_channels nor ants_humans; 'ants webhook serve' refuses credentials naming another user, a human's, or ones that do not allow the configured destination.

An exec or http sink gets each notice as one JSON object of version 1: kind (approval, escalation, completion or test), id, human, title, text, urgent, sent_at and links (one per offered verdict with public_url), plus ant, thread, request, seq, tool, options and expires_at for an approval, ant, thread, reason, stuck and level for an escalation and ant and thread for a completion; later versions only add fields and kinds, readers ignore unknown kinds, and a breaking change raises version.

A [[webhook]] entry's optional allow (tool rules, checked at load) narrows the tool rules of the threads it starts; without it the receiving daemons narrow them to read-only rules, and allow = ["*"] opts out.

'ants webhook serve' redacts the tool requests, escalations and replies its notices and approval pages carry, by the daemon's secret patterns and the secret-named variables of its own environment, whatever the ants' redact setting.

With escalations, ants webhook serve pushes a human's messages still waiting 15 minutes for an ant absent from the roster for 15 minutes as one notice of kind unserved (ant, messages) naming ants withdraw, once across services and ants inbox -f via the <human>.unserved.<id> marker; a snooze or quiet hours hold it until they end.

'ants webhook serve' answers 202 only after the hub's stream acknowledged the event, and 503 with Retry-After while NATS is unreachable or does not store it, keeping nothing locally; bodies are limited to 256 KiB (413), requests to 15 s and to 64 at once (503 beyond).

An event is identified by its configured id (a header, a JSON pointer or the body's SHA-256), published with Nats-Msg-Id 'webhook.<webhook>.<hash>' and recorded in KV ants_webhooks (created by 'ants init') for 7 days, so a retry in that time, also after an ingress restart, answers 200 with duplicate true and delivers nothing new.

A channel webhook's post mentions nobody, so the channel's messenger triages it, or the users its config lists, or with broadcast = true every member of the channel when the event is accepted; mentions are never taken from the event.
A webhook is no human: its messages and posts never renew a thread's turn budget or allowance, and escalations on its threads go to the owner its config names, else the daemon's default human.

An ant's reply to a webhook's message goes to the thread's owner as a reply to a human when the owner is a human, else nowhere: the daemon logs it and acks the message, and never sends it to the webhook's inbox.

'ants webhook serve' notifies each [[human]] of its config of pending tool requests and of escalations reaching its inbox through its ntfy, Slack or Telegram sinks, reading as that human its durable consumer 'notify-<human>' so several processes send each event once; requests already decided or expired are skipped, and a failing sink is logged without its URL or token and never stops the others.

comments.text:
Findings (details and configs in docs/transport.md). Verified with nats-server 2.15.3, async-nats 0.52, Caddy 2.11.9, all on loopback:
- ants ask/watch/init over wss://localhost/nats through Caddy reverse_proxy to a no_tls websocket listener: works, with and without JWT creds (operator mode). nats-server websocket accepts any path; a path ending /leafnode is a leaf. async-nats sends path+query unchanged, cannot add headers.
- Private CA: SSL_CERT_FILE=ca.pem works (rustls-native-certs); no ants flag needed. Without it: UnknownIssuer.
- Leaf remote wss:// through Caddy: works (leaf requests /nats/leafnode). Leaf through an HTTP CONNECT forward proxy (remote proxy { url }) + wss: works. async-nats has no HTTP proxy support, so ants itself cannot go through a forward proxy.
- JetStream API across a leaf without JS is denied ($JS.API.>): ants init on the leaf -> 'jetstream unavailable'. Fixes verified: hub jetstream domain + clients using with_domain ($JS.hub.API), or deprecated leaf default_js_domain {acct: ""}.
- Hub must set leafnodes { no_advertise: true }: otherwise a leaf reconnects to the hub's advertised internal address, bypassing the forwarder.
- Reconnect: proxy restart and forwarder drop recover within the 4 s back-off; durable consumer resumes. Silent link (SIGSTOP proxy) detected after 177 s with the default 60 s ping, 56 s with 20 s (now set in bus::connect). A message delivered into the dead connection's pull request redelivers only after ack_wait.
- Dev Tunnels HTTPS port as wss: only with anonymous port access (NATS JWT as real auth). Private tunnels need X-Tunnel-Authorization header or cookie; no query token (microsoft/dev-tunnels#478); neither async-nats nor leaf remotes can send headers. Not run (devtunnel login needed).
- No proxy blocked the WebSocket upgrade; TLS-inspecting proxies not reproduced.

Preserve existing thread ownership and escalation semantics; messenger triage remains responsible for unaddressed human and webhook posts.
design: Retain the human/ant identity distinction only where execution or delivery requires it. Extend existing channel commands, channel-manager validation and mention routing rather than introducing a separate human-only membership API. Define mixed and human-only mention handling explicitly so human mentions neither invoke an agent nor accidentally trigger messenger triage. Before implementation, use bd spec change for requirements that currently assume ant-only membership or forbid adding humans, especially ants-2mfe.37; review ants-2mfe.4, ants-2mfe.35, ants-2mfe.36 and ants-2mfe.42. Broader changes to channel-owner or messenger eligibility are not implied by participant parity.
title: Unify human and ant channel membership and mentions

acceptance_criteria: An authenticated webhook can durably enqueue an event for a configured ant and trigger normal processing. A channel webhook preserves normal mention/messenger routing; explicit broadcast wakes current members without waking unrelated ants. Invalid authentication or an unauthorized destination is rejected without enqueueing. Retrying the same event does not enqueue duplicate work, including after an ingress restart. Accepted events survive restart and transient NATS unavailability; no success response precedes durable acceptance. Webhook credentials cannot modify channel membership or impersonate a human. Focused integration tests cover routing, authorization, duplicate delivery and restart recovery. README documents configuration, request format, delivery semantics and identity/ownership rules.

comments.text: Implemented on fleet/caps (b63cf06), not yet merged. Design: (1) Per-prompt limits on every harness (harness.rs): wall clock (prompt_timeout_secs / --prompt-timeout-secs, default 1800) and distinct ACP ToolCall ids (max_tool_calls / --max-tool-calls, default 300); 0 = no limit. On a cut: CancelNotification, pending permission requests answered Cancelled, 30 s grace, otherwise the harness is stopped and the session resumes on the next message. (2) Spend caps (caps.rs Ledger): max_thread_tokens/max_thread_cost per thread since the human's last message, max_daily_tokens/max_daily_cost per persona per UTC day. Inputs: usage_update cost (cumulative per session; the increase is computed against the last reading of the same session) and PromptResponse.usage.total_tokens (feature unstable_end_turn_token_usage). Stored in KV ants_sessions under <persona>.<thread>.spend and <persona>.day.<YYYY-MM-DD> (30-day TTL), so spend survives restarts. All no-ops without caps, and for copilot, which reports no usage. (3) On a limit or cap: the reply carries partial text plus an '[ants] <limit>; the prompt was cancelled.' notice, and the thread escalates to the human through the turn-budget path (Inbox::escalate, '<why>; needs a decision. Last message from X'), except when the human sent the message (the notice reaches the human directly). While a cap is reached, later messages are escalated without prompting. Resets: a human message gives a fresh thread allowance; daily caps reset at 00:00 UTC or when the daemon restarts with a higher cap, and a human message does not lift them. Spec requirement: ants-0mi.12.

title: Token and cost caps per persona and thread

description: The terminal interface.
title: Command-line interface
'ants ask' sends to the persona named by a leading @persona, and to the messenger otherwise.
contrib/skills/ants/SKILL.md teaches a coding agent to message personas as the CLI's human through the CLI, without consuming other threads' unread replies.
The CLI acts as the human its credentials name, or 'human' without credentials, and registers that human in ants_humans when it connects.
'ants roster' shows each persona's escalation chain, leader first, and '--json' carries it as escalate_to.

'ants watch' prints an envelope carrying an escalation with its level, reason (and request id for a tool request), stuck persona and thread, leader and the personas visited, and an agent's approval decision in place of the envelope's text.

'ants approve' lists pending permission requests and answers them; every human sees every request and the first decision wins, a human's stored on the request's decision subject or an agent's from the requester's escalate_to, read back from the requester's inbox, so a request an agent decided first is not listed and a human answering it is told who decided it.

'ants persona add NAME' generates the persona's user NKey on its machine, keeps the seed there (0600, never sent), appends its [[persona]] entry to the config file without altering the existing text, and prints the public key until '--jwt' or '--enroll' completes the .creds file.

'ants auth user NAME --public-key U...' signs a user JWT for a public key generated elsewhere, with the rights it would give a key it generated, and prints it; 'ants persona add --jwt' accepts it only if it names the persona, is issued to the local public key and is signed by its issuer.

'ants enroll list/approve NAME/reject NAME' on the machine holding the account key lists the enrollment requests heard, signs the persona's requested key with the rights of 'ants auth user' and answers it, or refuses it; approve needs --public-key when several keys ask for the same persona.
'ants ask' sends to the ant named by a leading @ant, and to the messenger otherwise.
'ants roster' lists registered ants and their state.
'ants ask --wait' prints the first reply on the thread.
contrib/skills/ants/SKILL.md teaches a coding agent to message ants as the CLI's human through the CLI, without consuming other threads' unread replies.
'ants roster' shows each ant's escalation chain, leader first, and '--json' carries it as escalate_to.

'ants watch' prints an envelope carrying an escalation with its level, reason (and request id for a tool request), stuck ant and thread, leader and the ants visited, and an agent's approval decision in place of the envelope's text.

'ants add NAME' generates the ant's user NKey on its machine, keeps the seed there (0600, never sent), appends its [[ant]] entry to the config file without altering the existing text, and prints the public key until '--jwt' or '--enroll' completes the .creds file.

'ants auth user NAME --public-key U...' signs a user JWT for a public key generated elsewhere, with the rights it would give a key it generated, and prints it; 'ants add --jwt' accepts it only if it names the ant, is issued to the local public key and is signed by its issuer.

'ants enroll list/approve NAME/reject NAME' on the machine holding the account key lists the enrollment requests heard, signs the ant's requested key with the rights of 'ants auth user' and answers it, or refuses it; approve needs --public-key when several keys ask for the same ant.

'ants tools list' lists pending tool requests (--follow keeps printing new ones), 'ants tools show ID' shows one, and 'ants tools approve ID [--always]' or 'ants tools reject ID' answers it; every human sees every request and the first decision wins, a human's stored on the request's decision subject or an agent's from the requester's escalate_to, read back from the requester's inbox, so a request an agent decided first is not listed and a human answering it is told who decided it.

Durations in CLI flags and config keys are named without a unit suffix (--idle-timeout, idle_timeout, --ttl) and written with units s, m, h or d, largest first, such as 90s, 10m or 1h30m, or a bare 0; a bare non-zero number is rejected.

'ants ask --wait' and 'ants post --wait' print the first reply on the thread (to the CLI's human for ask, by someone other than the poster for post) and exit, '--follow' prints every later reply until the timeout or Ctrl-C, '--timeout DURATION' bounds either (no default), and a '--wait' that times out exits non-zero.

ants harness check and ants harness prompt run the harness named by --harness, else the config file's top-level harness, else copilot, resolved through the registry of the file named by --config or ANTS_CONFIG.
'ants watch' prints ants traffic live, filterable by subject.

Durations in CLI flags, config keys and MCP tool arguments are named without a unit suffix (--idle-timeout, idle_timeout, --ttl, the timeout of ask_agent and route) and written with units s, m, h or d, largest first, such as 90s, 10m or 1h30m, or a bare 0; a bare non-zero number is rejected.

'ants thread list' lists the threads with messages stored within --since (default 24h, 0 for all the stream keeps): id, owner, users and channels, first and last time, message count and opening line, the most recently active last, up to --limit (default 50); --ant, --owner and --grep TEXT (case-insensitive, in any message's text, printing the matching line) select threads, and --json prints one thread per line.

'ants thread show THREAD' prints every message stored on the thread in stream order (inbox messages either way, channel posts, notes, escalations, mentions, tool requests and decisions, dead letters) with time, kind, sender, recipient and text, reading from the thread's start when its id is a time-ordered UUID, else from --since or all the stream keeps; --json prints one entry per line.
'ants thread' reads the stream by message gets with a human's credentials, consuming, acking and marking read nothing, and refuses an ant's credentials.

'ants cancel ANT THREAD' with a human's credentials asks the daemons of ANT to cancel the prompt running on THREAD, prints that it did once one daemon answers that it cancelled it, and exits non-zero when every daemon that answers runs no prompt there (after a 500ms grace for the others) or none answers within 5s; an ant's credentials are refused.

'ants spend' reports, with human credentials, the tokens and cost each ant spent in UTC days over the last --days (default 7, today included), for one ANT also each thread's since a human's last message on it, and with --thread each ant's on that thread, as spent/cap against the caps the local config file sets for the ants it lists; '--json' prints one object per line.

Every device of a human sees every reply to it: 'ants inbox' shows what the human has not read on any device and marks it read on all of them (unless --peek) without consuming it, and 'ants inbox --follow' on each device shows every new reply, as 'ants ask --wait' marks its reply read on all devices.

Each 'ants auth user NAME --human' issues credentials for a new device of the human, with a generated id never reused, carried in the user JWT, and an optional --label; 'ants auth devices NAME' lists the devices (id or legacy, label, key, issue time, revoked), 'ants auth rename NAME DEVICE LABEL' relabels one and 'ants auth revoke NAME --device DEVICE' revokes it alone, DEVICE being an id, a key or a label no other device of the human has, an ambiguous label refused with the ids it names.

'ants add' that completes an ant's credentials reloads the daemon service scripts/install-units.sh installed for its config file (launchctl kill SIGHUP gui/<uid>/ants.daemon on macOS, systemctl --user reload ants-daemon on Linux) when that service runs, says so, and otherwise prints the commands that reload it by hand; a service of another config file is left alone.

Every command but 'ants daemon' and 'ants add' takes the --nats, --creds and --js-domain that neither a flag nor its environment variable sets from the [cli] section of the config file named by ANTS_CONFIG (default ~/.ants/config.toml, read only if it exists), else its top-level nats and js_domain (never an ant's creds), else the built-in default, and fails on an unreadable file or a malformed [cli], nats or js_domain.
'ants approve' lists pending permission requests and answers them.

While 'ants inbox --follow' without --thread or 'ants tools list --follow' runs on a device with an id, the CLI keeps that device's presence for escalations or tool requests in ants_presence and deletes it when the follow ends; a legacy device records none, and credentials without presence rights get a warning and follow without it.

A CLI command's first connection with a human's credentials, or none, does what 'ants init' does: one concurrent round of stream infos of ANTS and the buckets the credentials may inspect, creating those missing and adding what an older version lacks while keeping other settings such as outbox sources, logging each change and warning that 'ants init' is needed for a change the credentials may not make; an ant's credentials check nothing.

'ants doctor' checks a machine's setup without changing it: config file, CLI credentials, server and JetStream domain, hub stream and buckets as far as the credentials may look, each ant's credentials and harness sign-in, the leaf node, its uplinks and outbox sourcing, and installed services; one line per check (ok, warn, fail, skip) with a fix command for each warning or failure, a reason for each skip, timeouts on network checks, non-zero exit on failure.

A publish on a subject no stream captures while the hub's JetStream still answers the user's own inbox consumer info (an ANTS stream missing or from an older version) fails naming 'ants init' with a human's credentials, from the CLI, daemons, webhooks and the channel manager alike; on a leaf node with an outbox the message waits there with a warning saying the same, once per process for each kind of subject.

'ants leaf config' that rewrites a leaf.conf reloads the leaf node service scripts/install-units.sh installed for that file (launchctl kill SIGHUP gui/<uid>/ants.nats on macOS, systemctl --user reload ants-nats on Linux) when that service runs, restarts it instead when the change is one nats-server does not reload (anything but uplinks added or dropped and their TLS settings), says so, and otherwise prints the commands that do it by hand; a service of another file is left alone.

'ants roster' shows each daemon's ants and permissions versions and flags live daemons running mixed versions; 'ants doctor' run as a human reports whether every running daemon, webhook, schedule and channel manager runs this permissions version so that service credentials may be renewed, and the renewal hints of outdated service credentials point to it.

'ants doctor' checks a machine's setup without changing it: config file, CLI credentials, server and JetStream domain, hub stream and buckets as far as the credentials may look, the hub's resolver given the team keys, each ant's credentials and harness sign-in, the leaf node, its uplinks and outbox sourcing, and installed services; one line per check (ok, warn, fail, skip) with a fix for each warning or failure, a reason for each skip, timeouts on network checks, non-zero exit on failure.

On macOS, scripts/install-units.sh also installs the launchd agent ants.logrotate, which at load and hourly, as the user and without signalling or restarting any service, copies each ~/Library/Logs/ants/*.log over 10 MiB to a gzipped numbered copy, keeping 5, and truncates it in place, the services writing on through the file launchd holds open in append mode.

'ants ask' to an ant no daemon serves now (not in ants_roster, stale, or its harness signed out) and 'ants channel create/set/add' naming one warn on stderr but go ahead, a missing ant also hinting at a misspelt name when ants_chains keeps no chain for it; with --wait or --follow 'ants ask' adds that the wait may not end until a daemon serves the ant, and a roster that cannot be read within 3s warns of nothing.

The THREAD of 'ants ask', 'ants inbox', 'ants post', 'ants notes', 'ants thread show' and 'ants cancel' is a whole thread id (a UUID, taken without any lookup), a unique start of one among the threads with messages the CLI's human sent or received stored in the last 7 days (an exact id among them wins), or 'last' for the thread of the latest such message; a start matching none or several is refused listing those threads, and only a human's credentials pick by a start or 'last'.
'ants roster' lists registered personas and their state.

While 'ants inbox --follow' without --thread or 'ants tools list --follow' runs on a device with an id, the CLI keeps that device's presence in ants_presence and deletes it when the follow ends: for tool requests with 'ants tools list --follow' or 'ants inbox --follow' without --json, for escalations with 'ants inbox --follow'; a legacy device records none, and credentials without presence rights get a warning and follow without it.

'ants inbox --follow' without --thread and --json also prints the pending tool requests of every ant with the commands answering them, then each new one and how each printed one ends: answered by a human, answered by an agent of the ant's escalate_to (named), or expired.

Once an approval makes 3 human-approved requests of an ant for the same exact allow rule (command, single absolute path, URL or title), counting those still in the ANTS stream, 'ants tools approve' prints the rule and approval notices mention it; 'ants tools approve ID --rule' checks the rule can be added before approving, then adds it to the ant's allow list in the config file, leaving the rest of the file unchanged, and reloads the daemon service.

'ants keys store' moves a .creds file's NKey seed into the OS credential store only once stored, read back and authenticated at --nats with the file as it is to be, else leaves file and store as they were, and refuses leaf uplink credentials; 'ants keys unstore' moves it back into the owner-only file before deleting the entry; 'ants keys remove' deletes the entry and the file, naming the revocation still needed.

'ants doctor' warns, as check 'ant NAME workdir' with the fix worktrees = true in the ant's [[ant]], for each config-file ant with max_harnesses above 1 and worktrees off whose workdir is inside a git work tree; other ants get no such line.

The THREAD of 'ants ask', 'inbox', 'post', 'notes', 'thread show', 'cancel', 'watch', 'spend --thread' and 'channel read --thread' is a whole thread id (a UUID, used without lookup), a unique start of one among threads with messages the CLI's human sent or received stored in the last 7 days, else any user's threads started then (an exact id wins), or 'last', the thread of the human's latest message; a start matching none or several is refused listing threads; only humans pick by start or 'last'.

'ants doctor' run as a human warns, as check 'consumers', when stream ANTS holds four fifths of the consumers it takes (its max_consumers, else 1000 on nats-server 2.15 or later), with 'ants init' as the fix below 10000 and a higher max_consumers otherwise; with an ant's credentials it skips the check.

'ants add NAME' generates the ant's user NKey on its machine, keeps the seed there (0600, or with --store-key only in the OS credential store, the waiting .nk then holding its public key alone; never sent), appends its [[ant]] entry to the config file without altering the existing text, and prints the public key until '--jwt' or '--enroll' completes the .creds file.

'ants add --store-key', 'ants auth user --store-key' and 'ants auth channel-manager --store-key' write new credentials whose seed is only in the OS credential store: stored and read back, then the .creds file naming it written once it authenticates at the server, or with a warning when none answers; a server refusing it or any other failure leaves no file and deletes what was stored.

'ants doctor' checks, as 'credentials key' and 'ant NAME key', each CLI or config-file ant .creds file naming a stored key: the OS credential store answers, holds the entry, and its seed is the key of the user JWT; a locked or unavailable store fails with the fix to unlock it, a missing or mismatched entry with restoring it from a backup or issuing the credentials again, and no output shows the seed.
'ants inbox' shows replies to the human that arrived while no CLI was running.

'ants thread list --escalated' keeps the threads whose escalation, other than a tool request's, reached a human with no human's message or post on the thread since, within --since, and prints under each when the first such escalation reached a human, to whom, and the escalation.

With human credentials and stderr on a terminal, 'ants ask' and 'ants post' with --wait or --follow keep one status line on stderr from the thread's status updates (not served, queued behind N, working, running a tool, waiting for approval with the ants tools approve command, harness signed out), cleared before any reply, log line or error is printed; off a terminal or with ant credentials nothing is shown.

'ants doctor' warns, as check 'consumers', when stream ANTS or the stream of a bucket every daemon watches (KV_ants_roster, KV_ants_channels, KV_ants_humans) holds four fifths of the consumers it takes (its max_consumers, else 1000 on nats-server 2.15 or later), with 'ants init' as the fix below 10000 and a higher max_consumers otherwise; with an ant's credentials, which get no stream info of ANTS, it skips ANTS.

'ants doctor' checks the webhooks' config file when it is there: each secret file present with mode 0600 (an unset secret_env warns), the file as 'ants webhook serve' reads it, and public_url reaching serve's approval page within the network timeout (a warning otherwise); with no such file it prints nothing about webhooks.

'ants completions SHELL' prints a bash, zsh or fish script (--install writes it where the shell loads it from) completing commands and flags plus ants, channels, recent threads, pending tool requests and dead letter sequence numbers looked up over NATS as the completed command line would connect; a lookup gives up within 2 seconds, prompts for nothing and completes nothing on any error.

'ants setup' brings up a single machine (a loopback nats-server with JetStream and its service, ants init, a config file serving the messenger and the ant of --ant/--workdir, the harness check, the daemon service and shell completions) then runs 'ants doctor'; a re-run overwrites no file and reports what already exists, --dry-run changes nothing and --no-services installs and starts no service.

'ants hook run --on EVENT -- CMD' runs CMD once per approval request, decision, dead letter, escalation, status update or roster put, with the event's JSON document on stdin, at most --concurrency at once and killed after --timeout; stored events resume from the observer's durable consumer and are acked once CMD ends whatever its exit, forged or unreadable documents are skipped and failures logged.

`ants signer`, on the machine holding the account key, signs a manager ant's request for a new ant at once when it fits the template policy of the signer's own config file, never the requesting machine's copy, and otherwise signs only once a human approves it through the tool approvals path.

`ants signer` counts a template's ants against max_ants from the live keys the team issued from it, and refuses outright forged requests, names of humans, reserved names, names another live key holds, managers added from a template, and more than 3 requests of one manager waiting for humans.
`ants tools approve --rule` writes no `allow` key into the entry of an ant added from a template, approving once and printing the rule for the template instead.
contrib/skills/ants/SKILL.md teaches a coding agent to message personas as the human through the CLI, without consuming other threads' unread replies.

'ants retire NAME' retires an ant added from a template, whichever manager added it, as retire_ant does, revoking its credentials and pushing the account when --dir holds the account key and otherwise printing the 'ants auth revoke --key' to run there; it refuses an ant not added from a template, pointing to editing the config file and 'ants auth revoke'.

ants react MESSAGE REACTION adds the CLI user's reaction to a message and --remove takes it back, printing whether anything changed; ants ask and ants post print 'message <id>' after 'thread <id>'; ants inbox and ants thread show give each message's id and group the reactions to it beneath it (JSON fields id and reactions), and ants watch of ants.> or > with human credentials prints reactions added and removed live.

The MCP tool react(reaction, message_id?, remove?) adds or removes the ant's reaction, to the message being handled on the thread when message_id is omitted, and send_message, ask_agent, route and check_inbox results name the message ids of what was sent or replied.

'ants ask' and 'ants post' take the message from the words (after a leading @ant for ask), else from --file PATH (stdin only with --file -, lines kept but trailing line breaks) or --edit (VISUAL, else EDITOR, else vi or notepad, run through the shell on a new owner-only temporary file removed afterwards); blank input, words with --file or --edit, both flags, and an editor exiting non-zero or not found send nothing and exit non-zero.

'ants thread search' prints, with human credentials, consuming or marking read nothing, the messages matching every filter given (--from, --to, --channel, --type of the 'thread show' kinds, case-insensitive --grep, --since inclusive and --until exclusive as durations, RFC 3339 times or UTC dates, default 24h before --until), reading only the subjects the filters can match from --since on, the latest --limit (default 50) oldest first with thread, kind, id and time; --json one per line.

ants notify snooze DURATION (1s to 365d) holds back the CLI human's notifications until then on all its devices, ants notify resume ends the snooze and ants notify status [--json] shows the snooze and muted threads still in force; each needs human credentials.

ants thread mute THREAD [--for DURATION] (default 30d, at most 365d) and ants thread unmute THREAD hold back or release every notification of the thread to the CLI's human on all its devices, changing the human's ants_notify key by compare-and-set so devices changing it at once keep each other's changes.
ants webhook notify-test HUMAN also prints the human's quiet hours, their zone, whether they hold now and what bypass lets through.

ants thread title THREAD [TEXT...] [--clear] sets, renames, prints or removes the thread's one title, shared by every human and settable by any human, a trimmed line of 1-120 characters without control characters; ants thread list shows it in a TITLE column (title in --json), ants thread show on a title: line under its header, and completion of THREAD as the thread's description.

ants thread pin, unpin, archive and unarchive THREAD mark a thread for the CLI's human on all its devices and for no other human, pinning unarchiving and archiving unpinning, each printing whether anything changed; archiving deletes no message, cancels no work and holds back no reply or notification.
'ants approve' lists pending permission requests and answers them; every human sees every request and the first decision wins.

ants thread list puts the human's pinned threads after the others and drops others first under --limit, and leaves its archived threads out unless a message was stored on one after it was archived, then listing it as archived+new (new_activity in --json) while it stays archived until archived again or unarchived; --pinned or --archived lists only those, read by default from the earliest one's start.

ants queue ANT lists the messages waiting for ANT with message ID, thread, sender, age and position, and ants withdraw ANT MESSAGE withdraws one not started yet, failing with the reason when ANT already started or finished it; both require human credentials.

ants dash shows the recent threads with the selected one's history, the ants' live progress and roster, and the pending tool requests, each opened in full and answered only after a confirmation key through the ants tools approve and reject path (first decision wins); it shows the connection state and the age of its reads, rereads after reconnecting, and without a terminal exits 1 naming the scriptable commands.

'ants roster' shows each ant's harness agent as name@version and notes a harness agent that live ants run at different versions on different machines; 'ants doctor' check 'harness versions' warns of the same, naming which ants run which version, and passes when the versions differ on one machine only.

'ants doctor' on the machine holding the team keys warns, as check 'team keys backup' with 'ants auth backup FILE' as the fix, when no backup of those keys is recorded or issued.jsonl or revoked.json changed since the last one; without the team keys it prints no such line.

'ants doctor' reports, as check 'storage', the JetStream usage of each store of the hub and of the leaf node it connects through against its limit, warning past [storage] warn_percent (default 80) with the streams using most and the setting to raise, naming the [storage] setting when the limit is unknown, and skipping with credentials that may not read the account's JetStream info.

ants thread title THREAD [TEXT...] [--clear] sets, renames, prints or removes the thread's one title, shared by every human and settable by any human, a trimmed line of 1-120 characters without control characters or Unicode line and paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029); ants thread list shows it in a TITLE column (title in --json), ants thread show on a title: line under its header, and completion of THREAD as the thread's description.

'ants watch' prints an envelope carrying an escalation with its level, reason (and request id for a tool request), stuck ant and thread, leader and the ants visited, and an ant's approval decision in place of the envelope's text.

'ants tools list' lists pending tool requests (--follow keeps printing new ones), 'ants tools show ID' shows one, and 'ants tools approve ID [--always]' or 'ants tools reject ID' answers it; every human sees every request and the first decision wins, a human's stored on the request's decision subject or an ant's from the requester's escalate_to, read back from the requester's inbox, so a request an ant decided first is not listed and a human answering it is told who decided it.

Durations in CLI flags, config keys and MCP tool arguments are named without a unit suffix (--idle-timeout, idle_timeout, --ttl, the timeout of ask_ant and route) and written with units s, m, h or d, largest first, such as 90s, 10m or 1h30m, or a bare 0; a bare non-zero number is rejected.
'ants inbox' shows replies to the CLI's human that arrived while no CLI was running.

'ants inbox --follow' without --thread and --json also prints the pending tool requests of every ant with the commands answering them, then each new one and how each printed one ends: answered by a human, answered by an ant of the ant's escalate_to (named), or expired.

The MCP tool react(reaction, message_id?, remove?) adds or removes the ant's reaction, to the message being handled on the thread when message_id is omitted, and send_message, ask_ant, route and check_inbox results name the message ids of what was sent or replied.

description: bus::caught_up_inbox reads back with STREAM.MSG.GET, which only a human's credentials allow (it takes any sequence). An ant's credentials read its inbox from the stream only through its inbox consumer, which its daemon owns, so ants ask --wait/--follow run with an ant's credentials on a leaf hears only what comes live. Needs a read of only its own inbox subjects from the stream (e.g. a per-waiter consumer whose name and filter the permissions can pin).

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-57e8b162
comments.text: Seen through a real Dev Tunnel (ants-qjf.8, docs/transport.md): killing the worker's devtunnel connect leaves the hub-side socket from devtunnel host open (>5 min), the pull request of the dead connection takes the next message, and the daemon (already reconnected) gets it only after the 5-minute ack_wait. A hub ping_interval <= 30 s bounds the stale connection; a shorter ack_wait bounds the message.

description: When a link goes silent, a message delivered into the dead connection's pull request is redelivered only after ACK_WAIT (5 min in daemon.rs). The daemon already sends progress every 60 s, so ack_wait of about 2-3x PROGRESS_EVERY would cut the stall without risking duplicates on long turns. Measured in ants-qjf.9 (docs/transport.md).
title: Shorten inbox ack_wait so messages lost on a dead link redeliver sooner

description: ants auth revoke pushes the account to the hub, but every leaf node needs the new server.conf copied and SIGHUP, or a revoked ant behind a leaf keeps working there. Evaluate the NATS account resolver (cache or full) on leaves so a pushed account reaches them, or have ants auth push target leaves too.
title: Propagate revocations to leaf nodes without copying server.conf by hand

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-6416fce2
comments.text: Implemented on branch fleet-vt0m (650926a, af7a69f, effc5c5): ants persona add NAME (seed generated and kept locally, [[persona]] appended to config, --jwt / --enroll complete the .creds), ants auth user --public-key (prints JWT), ants auth enroll NAME (expiring creds: pub ants.enroll.<name>, sub ants.enroll.<name>.reply), ants enroll list/approve/reject (self-issued 10-min approver creds from account.nk). Requests are core NATS, not stored; requester repeats every 5s, approver listens 6s. Pickup: restart daemon (printed). Specs ants-ved.15-17, ants-h0k.27-28. Follow-ups: ants-je3b (SIGHUP reload), ants-3re2 (enrollment/leaf uplink+outbox), ants-m3k0 (human approvers).

description: Creating an agent today takes 'ants auth user' on the machine holding account.nk, copying the .creds, editing ~/.ants/config.toml by hand and running ants daemon. Make it one command on the agent's machine, without moving any seed.
design:
Design sketch:
- 'ants persona add NAME --workdir ... [harness, model, ...]' writes the [[persona]] entry and generates the persona's user NKey locally; the seed never leaves the machine.
- Credentials: the request carries only the public key. Signing needs account.nk, so the approver runs on the key machine (or a small signer service there). Two paths: (a) out of band: print the public key; 'ants auth user NAME --public-key U...' prints the JWT; 'ants persona add --jwt' completes the .creds; (b) over NATS: an enrollment credential (publish only ants.enroll.<name>, subscribe its reply) sends the request; 'ants enroll list/approve/reject' on the key machine signs and replies.
- Then the daemon picks up the persona (start it, or the running daemon reloads its config).
- Open: --js-domain and leaf uplink updates (ants auth leaf / ants leaf outbox) for the new persona; enrollment credential issuance and expiry; whether multi-human (ants-548b) humans may approve.
title: Enroll a persona from any machine: ants persona add

Links the hub cannot record are kept in the leaf outbox (ants.out.links.<key>) and ants_links sources them from the intake per ant (ants leaf outbox). Spec ants-h0k.44 changed to ants-h0k.54. Commit 9998ee8 on fleet-wjd1.
description: escalation.rs builds escalation envelopes to chain members (to_chain) and the level notices with Envelope::on_thread(...).with_creator(...) but no origin_thread. On a thread spun off a channel thread (no channel post started it), the receiving daemon's Claims::spun_off_creator then drops the creator, so a chain member answering or escalating further sees no creator. Carrying origin_thread there would also need the link recorded (links::pass_on), as the escalation is sent through Escalator's send, not the MCP outbox. Also: links passed on while a leaf's uplink is down are not recorded (the put fails), so those recipients drop the creator.
title: Escalation envelopes on a spun-off thread carry creator without origin_thread

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-abe4085b
comments.text: Implemented on fleet/dupes (701cc7a). Design: new KV bucket ants_attempts (file, max_age 30 d like the stream, history 1), key <persona>.<stream seq>, value {message: envelope id, reply?}. A marker naming another envelope id is ignored (a recreated stream reuses sequences). Flow in handle()/answer(): read marker -> none: put started, prompt as sent; started: prompt with the [ants] cut-off warning prepended (every redelivery after a started attempt, failed/naked or crashed); replied: re-send the recorded reply and ack without prompting. After the prompt the reply is recorded in the marker BEFORE publishing; replies (and turn-budget escalations) are published with Nats-Msg-Id reply-<persona>-<seq> / escalation-<persona>-<seq>, so a re-send within the 2 min duplicate window stores nothing; beyond it the same envelope (same id) is stored again. Marker deleted after ack and after a dead letter. Overdue delivery with a recorded reply sends it instead of dead-lettering. In-memory in-hand guard (0mi.10) kept. Permissions: persona gets STREAM.INFO, DIRECT.GET and $KV put/delete on its own keys only; human creates the bucket (ants init). Upgrade: rerun ants init and reissue persona/leaf creds. Spec: ants-0mi.13. Residual window: a crash after the harness answered but before the reply is recorded re-prompts (with the warning).

description: A crash after a harness ran tools but before the ack redelivers the inbox message and replays the prompt, so external effects can repeat. Store a 'started' marker (persona + stream sequence) before prompting; a redelivery that finds one is prompted with a warning that tools may have already run (the harness session is resumed with session/load), and a message whose reply is already stored is acked without prompting again.
title: Warn a redelivered prompt that its first attempt may already have run tools

close_reason: A climbing member sends the stuck persona a notice carrying the new escalation; its daemon acks it unprompted and adopts the level with a fresh deadline (Escalator::took_climb, Ledger::climbed); the higher leader's answer also adopts it. description: When a chain member (lead) is stuck working on dev-a's escalation, lead's daemon sends it one level higher (level 2, from lead to boss) and boss answers lead, renewing lead's thread. dev-a's own Pending stays at level 1, so dev-a's next spend climbs from level 1 again and boss gets a second level-2 escalation, from dev-a. comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-003b2bf9
comments.text:
ants-9lar (branch fleet-windows, commits afd9acb 79131ff 4a0a810) makes the workspace build for Windows: clippy -D warnings clean for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and -msvc, ants.exe linked with llvm-mingw from macOS; CI gains a windows-latest job (clippy, the MCP named pipe test, release build). Not run on Windows here: no Windows machine or Wine (arm64 Mac without Rosetta). Still to verify on a real Windows 10/11 machine:

BUILD: install Rust 1.100+ and Visual Studio Build Tools (C++ workload), then in a checkout: `cargo build --release` (target\release\ants.exe), or `cargo install --locked --path crates/ants`. Alternative: cross-build from macOS/Linux with `rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and mingw-w64 on PATH: `cargo build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`. Also run `cargo test -p ants-daemon --lib -- mcp::tests::the_socket_serves_the_tools_after_the_token keystore` there.

1. Key store round trip (interactive desktop logon with password, nats-server running, human creds issued with `ants auth user NAME --human`):
   - `ants --nats URL --creds C:\path\me.creds keys store` -> "seed moved to the OS credential store, key U..."; the file now holds the JWT and the key reference only; `cmdkey /list:ants:*` (or Credential Manager > Windows Credentials) shows generic credential `ants:U...`, persistence Local computer.
   - `ants --nats URL --creds C:\path\me.creds whoami` (or `ants doctor`) connects using the stored seed; `ants doctor` reports the stored key OK.
   - `ants --nats URL --creds ... keys store` again -> "already in the OS credential store".
   - `ants --creds ... keys unstore` -> seed back in the file, credential `ants:U...` gone (`cmdkey /list:ants:*`).
   - store again, then `ants --creds ... keys remove` -> file and credential both gone.
2. A connection with a .creds naming a stored key: `ants add dev-a --store-key ...` (or keys store on an ant's creds), then `ants daemon --config ...` serving dev-a connects and answers `ants ask dev-a "hi" --wait`; delete the credential with `cmdkey /delete:ants:U...` and restart: the daemon must stop dev-a at once naming the missing entry.
3. SSH key-auth session: enable OpenSSH Server, log in with a public key (no password), run `ants --creds <stored file> whoami` -> must fail with "Windows Credential Manager: ... (os error 1312): this logon session has no credential set, as with an SSH session authenticated by key, ... keep the seed in the file (`ants keys unstore`)". Logging in over SSH with the password should instead succeed.
4. Service as another account: `schtasks /Create /SC ONSTART /RU OTHERUSER /RP * /TN ants-test /TR "C:\...\ants.exe --creds C:\...\stored.creds daemon --config ..."` (another account, or SYSTEM via /RU SYSTEM): it must not read the first user's credential (no entry / error 1312 named); then as the same user with "Run whether user is logged on or not" and the password stored it should work, and with "Do not store password" it fails with 1312.
5. Windows-specific bits of ants-9lar worth checking in the same session: a harness without HTTP MCP (e.g. one configured in [harnesses.X] lacking HTTP MCP) gets tools through `ants mcp --socket \\.\pipe\ants-mcp-<hex>`; another local user cannot open the pipe (e.g. from a second account: `[System.IO.Pipes.NamedPipeClientStream]::new('.', 'ants-mcp-<hex>').Connect(1000)` -> access denied); `copilot` installed by npm (copilot.cmd) starts as the harness; Ctrl-C / closing the console stops the daemon cleanly.
